अलक्ष्मीमग्रतः सृष्ट्वा पश्चात्पद्मां जनार्दनः ॥
2.6.m: and unrighteousness into one portion, [he of] great splendour. / Having created Alakṣmī first, Janārdana afterwards [created] Padmā.

2.6.s:
jyeṣṭhā tena samākhyātā alakṣmīrdvijasattamāḥ /
amṛtodbhavavelāyāṃ viṣānantaramulbaṇāt //
2.6.d:
ज्येष्ठा तेन समाख्याता अलक्ष्मीर्द्विजसत्तमाः ।
अमृतोद्भववेलायां विषानन्तरमुल्बणात् ॥
2.6.m: Therefore Alakṣmī is declared to be Jyeṣṭhā, O best of the twice-born. / At the time of the emergence of the nectar, directly after the dreadful poison,

2.6.s:
aśubhā sā tathotpannā jyeṣṭhā iti ca vai śrutam /
tataḥ śrīśca samutpannā padmā viṣṇuparigrahaḥ //
2.6.d:
अशुभा सा तथोत्पन्ना ज्येष्ठा इति च वै श्रुतम् ।
ततः श्रीश्च समुत्पन्ना पद्मा विष्णुपरिग्रहः ॥
2.6.m: that inauspicious one was thus born, and is traditionally heard of as Jyeṣṭhā. / After that Śrī Padmā was born, the consort of Viṣṇu.

2.6.s:
duḥsaho nāma viprarṣirupayeme 'śubhāṃ tadā /
jyeṣṭhāṃ tāṃ paripūrṇo 'sau manasā vīkṣya dhiṣṭhitām //
2.6.d:
दुःसहो नाम विप्रर्षिरुपयेमे ऽशुभां तदा ।
ज्येष्ठां तां परिपूर्णो ऽसौ मनसा वीक्ष्य धिष्ठिताम् ॥
2.6.m: Then a brāhmaṇa sage named Duḥsaha married that inauspicious one, / Jyeṣṭhā, seeing her positioned [there], he being fulfilled in mind.

2.6.s:
lokaṃ cacāraṃ hṛṣṭātmā tayā saha munistadā /
yasmin ghoṣo hareścaiva harasya ca mahātmanaḥ //
2.6.d:
लोकं चचारं हृष्टात्मा तया सह मुनिस्तदा ।
यस्मिन् घोषो हरेश्चैव हरस्य च महात्मनः ॥
2.6.m: Then, joyful in spirit, that sage roamed the world together with her. / Wherever there was the sound of Hari and of the great-souled Hara,

2.6.s:
vedaghoṣastathā viprā homadhūmastathaiva ca /
bhasmāṅgino vā yatrāsaṃstatra tatra bhayārditā //
2.6.d:
वेदघोषस्तथा विप्रा होमधूमस्तथैव च ।
भस्माङ्गिनो वा यत्रासंस्तत्र तत्र भयार्दिता ॥
2.6.m: as well as the sound of the Vedas, O brāhmaṇas, and likewise sacrificial smoke, / or wherever people had their bodies smeared with sacred ash, afflicted with fear there and then,

2.6.s:
pidhāya karṇau saṃyāti dhāvamānā itastataḥ /
jyeṣṭhāmevaṃvidhāṃ dṛṣṭvā duḥsaho mohamāgataḥ //
2.6.d:
पिधाय कर्णौ संयाति धावमाना इतस्ततः ।
ज्येष्ठामेवंविधां दृष्ट्वा दुःसहो मोहमागतः ॥
2.6.m: covering her ears she departed, running here and there. / Seeing Jyeṣṭhā like this, Duḥsaha became bewildered.

2.6.s:
tayā saha vanaṃ gatvā cacāra sa mahāmuniḥ /
tapo mahadvane ghore yāti kanyā pratigraham //
2.6.d:
तया सह वनं गत्वा चचार स महामुनिः ।
तपो महद्वने घोरे याति कन्या प्रतिग्रहम् ॥
2.6.m: Having gone with her into the forest, that great sage wandered. / Performing great asceticism in the terrible forest, [thinking,] 'I accepted a maiden,

2.6.s:
na kariṣyāmi cetyuktvā pratijñāya ca tāmṛṣiḥ /
yogajñānaparaḥ śuddho yatra yogīśvaro muniḥ //
2.6.d:
न करिष्यामि चेत्युक्त्वा प्रतिज्ञाय च तामृषिः ।
योगज्ञानपरः शुद्धो यत्र योगीश्वरो मुनिः ॥
2.6.m: and now I will not abandon her', having made that vow to her, the sage, / devoted to knowledge of yoga and pure, saw the great-souled Mārkaṇḍeya,

2.6.s:
tatrāyāntaṃ mahātmānaṃ mārkaṇḍeyamapaśyata /
praṇipatya mahātmānaṃ duḥsaho munimabravīt //
2.6.d:
तत्रायान्तं महात्मानं मार्कण्डेयमपश्यत ।
प्रणिपत्य महात्मानं दुःसहो मुनिमब्रवीत् ॥
2.6.m: a sage and master of yoga, approaching there. / Having bowed down to that great-souled one, Duḥsaha spoke to the sage:

2.6.s:
bhāryeyaṃ bhagavanmahyaṃ na sthāsyati kathañcana /
kiṃ karomīti viprarṣe hyanayā saha bhāryayā //
2.6.d:
भार्येयं भगवन्मह्यं न स्थास्यति कथञ्चन ।
किं करोमीति विप्रर्षे ह्यनया सह भार्यया ॥
2.6.m: O venerable one, this wife of mine will not stay [anywhere] at all. / What should I do, O brāhmaṇa sage, with this wife?

2.6.s:
praviśāmi tathā kutra kuto na praviśāmyaham /
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
śṛṇu duḥsaha sarvatra akīrtiraśubhānvitā //
2.6.d:
प्रविशामि तथा कुत्र कुतो न प्रविशाम्यहम् ।
मार्कण्डेय उवाच
शृणु दुःसह सर्वत्र अकीर्तिरशुभान्विता ॥
2.6.m: Where then should I enter, and where should I not enter? / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Listen, Duḥsaha, everywhere she is ill fame and endowed with misfortune;

2.6.s:
alakṣmīratulā ceyaṃ jyeṣṭhā ityabhiśabditā /
nārāyaṇaparā yatra vedamārgānusāriṇaḥ //
2.6.d:
अलक्ष्मीरतुला चेयं ज्येष्ठा इत्यभिशब्दिता ।
नारायणपरा यत्र वेदमार्गानुसारिणः ॥
2.6.m: she is peerless Alakṣmī, declared by the name Jyeṣṭhā. / Where people devoted to Nārāyaṇa, followers of the Vedic path,

2.6.s:
rudrabhaktā mahātmāno bhasmoddhūlitavigrahāḥ /
sthitā yatra janā nityaṃ mā viśethāḥ kathañcana //
2.6.d:
रुद्रभक्ता महात्मानो भस्मोद्धूलितविग्रहाः ।
स्थिता यत्र जना नित्यं मा विशेथाः कथञ्चन ॥
2.6.m: great-souled devotees of Rudra, their bodies smeared with sacred ash, / are permanently situated, never enter there at all.

2.6.s:
nārāyaṇa hṛṣīkeśa puṇḍarīkākṣa mādhava /
acyutānanta govinda vāsudeva janārdana //
2.6.d:
नारायण हृषीकेश पुण्डरीकाक्ष माधव ।
अच्युतानन्त गोविन्द वासुदेव जनार्दन ॥
2.6.m: [Where people say,] 'O Nārāyaṇa, Hṛṣīkeśa, Lotus-eyed One, Mādhava! / O Acyuta, Ananta, Govinda, Vāsudeva, Janārdana!'

2.6.s:
rudra rudreti rudreti śivāya ca namo namaḥ /
namaḥ śivatarāyeti śaṅkarāyeti sarvadā //
2.6.d:
रुद्र रुद्रेति रुद्रेति शिवाय च नमो नमः ।
नमः शिवतरायेति शङ्करायेति सर्वदा ॥
2.6.m: [and where they say,] 'O Rudra, Rudra, Rudra! Homage, homage to Śiva! / Homage to the more auspicious one, to Śaṅkara always!'

2.6.s:
mahādeva mahādeva mahādeveti kīrtayet /
umāyāḥ pataye caiva hiraṇyapataye sadā //
2.6.d:
महादेव महादेव महादेवेति कीर्तयेत् ।
उमायाः पतये चैव हिरण्यपतये सदा ॥
2.6.m: [and where they] glorify, 'O Mahādeva, Mahādeva, Mahādeva! / And to the husband of Umā, to the lord of gold always,

2.6.s:
hiraṇyabāhave tubhyaṃ vṛṣāṅkāya namo namaḥ /
nṛsiṃhavāmanācintya mādhaveti ca ye janāḥ //
2.6.d:
हिरण्यबाहवे तुभ्यं वृषाङ्काय नमो नमः ।
नृसिंहवामनाचिन्त्य माधवेति च ये जनाः ॥
2.6.m: to you who have golden arms, to the one who has a bull as his emblem, homage, homage!' / And the people who [say,] 'O Narasiṃha, Vāmana, Inconceivable One, Mādhava!'—

2.6.s:
vakṣyanti satataṃ hṛṣṭā brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyāstathā /
vaiśyāḥ śūdrāśca ye nityaṃ teṣāṃ dhanagṛhādiṣu /
ārāme caiva goṣṭheṣu na viśethāḥ kathañcana //
2.6.d:
वक्ष्यन्ति सततं हृष्टा ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रियास्तथा ।
वैश्याः शूद्राश्च ये नित्यं तेषां धनगृहादिषु ।
आरामे चैव गोष्ठेषु न विशेथाः कथञ्चन ॥
2.6.m: brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, / vaiśyas, and śūdras who will speak [thus] constantly with delight—never enter at all into their wealth, houses, / gardens, and cow-pens.

2.6.s:
jvālāmālākarālaṃ ca sahasrādityasannibham /
cakraṃ viṣṇoratīvograṃ teṣāṃ hanti sadāśubham //
2.6.d:
ज्वालामालाकरालं च सहस्रादित्यसन्निभम् ।
चक्रं विष्णोरतीवोग्रं तेषां हन्ति सदाशुभम् ॥
2.6.m: The terrifying discus of Viṣṇu, surrounded by a garland of flames and resembling a thousand suns, / exceedingly fierce, always destroys their misfortune.

2.6.s:
svāhākāro vaṣaṭkāro gṛhe yasmin hi vartate /
taddhitvā cānyamāgaccha samāghoṣetha yatra vā //
2.6.d:
स्वाहाकारो वषट्कारो गृहे यस्मिन् हि वर्तते ।
तद्धित्वा चान्यमागच्छ समाघोषेथ यत्र वा ॥
2.6.m: In whatever house the utterance svāhā and the utterance vaṣaṭ exist, / leaving that, go elsewhere; or wherever there is chanting [of the Vedas],

2.6.s:
vedābhyāsaratā nityaṃ nityakarmaparāyaṇāḥ /
vāsudevārcanaratā dūratastānvisarjayet //
2.6.d:
वेदाभ्यासरता नित्यं नित्यकर्मपरायणाः ।
वासुदेवार्चनरता दूरतस्तान्विसर्जयेत् ॥
2.6.m: [where people are] constantly devoted to the study of the Vedas, devoted to their daily rituals, / and devoted to the worship of Vāsudeva, leave them far away.

2.6.s:
agnihotraṃ gṛhe yeṣāṃ liṅgārcā vā gṛheṣu ca /
vāsudevatanurvāpi caṇḍikā yatra tiṣṭhati //
2.6.d:
अग्निहोत्रं गृहे येषां लिङ्गार्चा वा गृहेषु च ।
वासुदेवतनुर्वापि चण्डिका यत्र तिष्ठति ॥
2.6.m: In whose house there is the agnihotra, or the worship of the liṅga in their homes, / or the image of Vāsudeva, or where Caṇḍikā abides,

2.6.s:
dūrato vraja tān hitvā sarvapāpavivarjitān /
nityanaimittikairyajñairyajanti ca maheśvaram //
2.6.d:
दूरतो व्रज तान् हित्वा सर्वपापविवर्जितान् ।
नित्यनैमित्तिकैर्यज्ञैर्यजन्ति च महेश्वरम् ॥
2.6.m: abandoning them, go far away from those freed from all sins. / Those who worship Maheśvara with regular and occasional sacrifices,

2.6.s:
tān hitvā vraja cānyatra duḥsahatvaṃ sahānayā /
śrotriyā brāhmaṇā gāvo guravo 'tithayaḥ sadā //
2.6.d:
तान् हित्वा व्रज चान्यत्र दुःसहत्वं सहानया ।
श्रोत्रिया ब्राह्मणा गावो गुरवो ऽतिथयः सदा ॥
2.6.m: leaving them, go elsewhere, O Duḥsaha, together with her. / Where learned brāhmaṇas, cows, preceptors, guests,

2.6.s:
rudrabhaktāśca pūjyante yairnityaṃ tānvivarjayet /
duḥsaha uvāca
yasminpraveśo yogyo me tadbrūhi munisattama //
2.6.d:
रुद्रभक्ताश्च पूज्यन्ते यैर्नित्यं तान्विवर्जयेत् ।
दुःसह उवाच
यस्मिन्प्रवेशो योग्यो मे तद्ब्रूहि मुनिसत्तम ॥
2.6.m: and devotees of Rudra are constantly honoured, avoid them. / Duḥsaha said: / Tell me that [place] where my entrance is suitable, O best of sages.

2.6.s:
tvadvākyādbhayanirmukto viśānmeṣāṃ gṛhe sadā /
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
na śrotriyā dvijā gāvo guravo 'tithayaḥ sadā /
yatra bhartā ca bhāryā ca parasparavirodhinau //
2.6.d:
त्वद्वाक्याद्भयनिर्मुक्तो विशान्मेषां गृहे सदा ।
मार्कण्डेय उवाच
न श्रोत्रिया द्विजा गावो गुरवो ऽतिथयः सदा ।
यत्र भर्ता च भार्या च परस्परविरोधिनौ ॥
2.6.m: Free from fear by your words, may I always enter their house. / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Where learned [brāhmaṇas], twice-born men, cows, preceptors, and guests are never [honoured], / where husband and wife are mutually hostile,

2.6.s:
sabhāryastvaṃ gṛhaṃ tasya viśethā bhayavarjitaḥ /
devadevo mahādevo rudrastribhuvaneśvaraḥ //
2.6.d:
सभार्यस्त्वं गृहं तस्य विशेथा भयवर्जितः ।
देवदेवो महादेवो रुद्रस्त्रिभुवनेश्वरः ॥
2.6.m: with your wife you may enter that person's house, free from fear. / Where the God of gods, Mahādeva, Rudra, the Lord of the three worlds,

2.6.s:
vinindyo yatra bhagavān viśasva bhayavarjitaḥ /
vāsudevaratirnāsti yatra nāsti sadāśivaḥ //
2.6.d:
विनिन्द्यो यत्र भगवान् विशस्व भयवर्जितः ।
वासुदेवरतिर्नास्ति यत्र नास्ति सदाशिवः ॥
2.6.m: the Lord, is reviled, enter free from fear. / Where there is no love for Vāsudeva, where Sadāśiva is absent,

2.6.s:
japahomādikaṃ nāsti bhasma nāsti gṛhe nṛṇām /
parvaṇyabhyarcanaṃ nāsti caturdaśyāṃ viśeṣataḥ //
2.6.d:
जपहोमादिकं नास्ति भस्म नास्ति गृहे नृणाम् ।
पर्वण्यभ्यर्चनं नास्ति चतुर्दश्यां विशेषतः ॥
2.6.m: where there is no recitation of mantras, oblations, and the like, where there is no sacred ash in the houses of men, / where there is no worship on auspicious days, especially on the fourteenth day,

2.6.s:
kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ ca rudrasya saṃdhyāyāṃ bhasmavarjitāḥ /
caturdaśyāṃ mahādevaṃ na yajanti ca yatra vai //
2.6.d:
कृष्णाष्टम्यां च रुद्रस्य संध्यायां भस्मवर्जिताः ।
चतुर्दश्यां महादेवं न यजन्ति च यत्र वै ॥
2.6.m: and on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, [where they do not worship] Rudra, where at the twilight they are without sacred ash, / and where they do not sacrifice to Mahādeva on the fourteenth day,

2.6.s:
viṣṇornāmavihinā ye saṃgatāśca durātmabhiḥ /
namaḥ kṛṣṇāya śarvāya śivāya parameṣṭhine //
2.6.d:
विष्णोर्नामविहिना ये संगताश्च दुरात्मभिः ।
नमः कृष्णाय शर्वाय शिवाय परमेष्ठिने ॥
2.6.m: those who are devoid of the name of Viṣṇu and associate with evil-minded people, / [where] brāhmaṇas and foolish people of wicked mind

2.6.s:
brāhmaṇāśca narā mūḍhā navadanti durātmakāḥ /
tatraiva satataṃ vatsa sabhāryastvaṃ samāvisa //
2.6.d:
ब्राह्मणाश्च नरा मूढा नवदन्ति दुरात्मकाः ।
तत्रैव सततं वत्स सभार्यस्त्वं समाविस ॥
2.6.m: do not say, 'Homage to Kṛṣṇa, to Śarva, to Śiva, to the Supreme Lord'— / right there constantly, my child, enter together with your wife.

2.6.s:
vedaghoṣo na yatrāsti gurupūjādayo na ca /
pitṛkarmavihīnāṃstu sabhāryastvaṃ samāviśa //
2.6.d:
वेदघोषो न यत्रास्ति गुरुपूजादयो न च ।
पितृकर्मविहीनांस्तु सभार्यस्त्वं समाविश ॥
2.6.m: Where there is no sound of the Vedas, nor worship of preceptors and the like, / enter together with your wife among those devoid of rites for the ancestors.

2.6.s:
rātrau rātrau gṛhe yasmin kalaho vartate mithaḥ /
anayā sārdhamaniśaṃ viśa tvaṃ bhayavarjitaḥ //
2.6.d:
रात्रौ रात्रौ गृहे यस्मिन् कलहो वर्तते मिथः ।
अनया सार्धमनिशं विश त्वं भयवर्जितः ॥
2.6.m: In whatever house there is mutual quarrelling night after night, / with her enter there incessantly, free from fear.

2.6.s:
liṅgārcanaṃ yasya nāsti yasya nāsti japādikam /
rudrabhaktirvinindā ca tatraiva viśa nirbhayaḥ //
2.6.d:
लिङ्गार्चनं यस्य नास्ति यस्य नास्ति जपादिकम् ।
रुद्रभक्तिर्विनिन्दा च तत्रैव विश निर्भयः ॥
2.6.m: Where there is no worship of the liṅga, where there is no recitation of mantras and the like, / and where there is censure of devotion to Rudra, enter right there without fear.

2.6.s:
atithiḥ śrotriyo vāpi gururvāvaiṣṇavopi vā /
na saṃti yadgṛhe gāvaḥ sabhāryastvaṃ samāviśa //
2.6.d:
अतिथिः श्रोत्रियो वापि गुरुर्वावैष्णवोपि वा ।
न संति यद्गृहे गावः सभार्यस्त्वं समाविश ॥
2.6.m: In whose house there is no guest, nor a learned brāhmaṇa, nor a preceptor, nor a Vaiṣṇava, / nor cows, enter [there] together with your wife.

2.6.s:
bālānāṃ prekṣamāṇānāṃ yatrādattvā tvabhakṣayan /
bhakṣyāṇi tatra saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sabhāryastvaṃ samāviśa //
2.6.d:
बालानां प्रेक्षमाणानां यत्रादत्त्वा त्वभक्षयन् ।
भक्ष्याणि तत्र संहृष्टः सभार्यस्त्वं समाविश ॥
2.6.m: Where they eat eatables without giving [any] to children who are watching, / enter there delighted, together with your wife.

2.6.s:
anabhyarcya mahādevaṃ vāsudevamathāpi vā /
ahutvā vidhivadyatra tatra nityaṃ samāviśa //
2.6.d:
अनभ्यर्च्य महादेवं वासुदेवमथापि वा ।
अहुत्वा विधिवद्यत्र तत्र नित्यं समाविश ॥
2.6.m: Where they do not worship Mahādeva or Vāsudeva, / and do not offer oblations according to rule, enter there constantly.

2.6.s:
pāpa karmaratā mūḍhā dayāhīnāḥ parasparam /
gṛhe yasminsamāsaṃte deśe vā tatra saṃviśa //
2.6.d:
पाप कर्मरता मूढा दयाहीनाः परस्परम् ।
गृहे यस्मिन्समासंते देशे वा तत्र संविश ॥
2.6.m: In whatever house or region there live fools devoted to sinful deeds / and lacking compassion for one another, enter there.

2.6.s:
prākārāgāravidhvaṃsā na caiveḍyā kuṭuṃbinī /
tadgṛhaṃ tu samāsādya vasa nityaṃ hi hṛṣṭadhīḥ //
2.6.d:
प्राकारागारविध्वंसा न चैवेड्या कुटुंबिनी ।
तद्गृहं तु समासाद्य वस नित्यं हि हृष्टधीः ॥
2.6.m: Where enclosures and houses are ruined and the mistress of the house is not respected, / reaching that house, dwell there constantly with a glad mind.

2.6.s:
yatra kaṇṭakino vṛkṣā yatra niṣpāvavallarī /
brahmavṛkṣaśca yatrāsti sabhāryāstvaṃ samāviśa //
2.6.d:
यत्र कण्टकिनो वृक्षा यत्र निष्पाववल्लरी ।
ब्रह्मवृक्षश्च यत्रास्ति सभार्यास्त्वं समाविश ॥
2.6.m: Where there are thorny trees, where there is the niṣpāva creeper, / and where the brahma-tree stands, enter there together with your wife.

2.6.s:
agastyārkādayo vāpi bandhujīvo gṛheṣu vai /
karavīro viśeṣeṇa nandyāvartamathāpi vā //
2.6.d:
अगस्त्यार्कादयो वापि बन्धुजीवो गृहेषु वै ।
करवीरो विशेषेण नन्द्यावर्तमथापि वा ॥
2.6.m: Or where the agastya, arka, and similar plants grow, or bandhujīva in the houses, / especially the oleander, or even the nandyāvarta,

2.6.s:
mallikā vā gṛhe yeṣāṃ sabhāryāstvaṃ samāviśa /
kanyā ca yatra vai vallī drohī vā ca jaṭī gṛhe //
2.6.d:
मल्लिका वा गृहे येषां सभार्यास्त्वं समाविश ।
कन्या च यत्र वै वल्ली द्रोही वा च जटी गृहे ॥
2.6.m: or jasmine in their houses, enter there together with your wife; / or where a maiden, a creeper, a traitor, or an ascetic with matted hair is in the house,

2.6.s:
bahulā kadalī yatra sabhāryastvaṃ samāviśa /
tālaṃ tamālaṃ bhallātaṃ tittiḍīkhaṇḍameva ca //
2.6.d:
बहुला कदली यत्र सभार्यस्त्वं समाविश ।
तालं तमालं भल्लातं तित्तिडीखण्डमेव च ॥
2.6.m: where there is an abundance of plantains, enter there together with your wife; / or [where there is] a palmyra palm, a tamāla, a Marking Nut tree, or a clump of tamarind,

2.6.s:
kadaṃbaḥ khādiraṃ vāpi sabhāryastvaṃ samāviśa /
nyagrodhaṃ vā gṛhe yeṣāmaśvatthaṃ cūtameva vā //
2.6.d:
कदंबः खादिरं वापि सभार्यस्त्वं समाविश ।
न्यग्रोधं वा गृहे येषामश्वत्थं चूतमेव वा ॥
2.6.m: a kadamba, or a catechu, enter there together with your wife; / or in the house of those who have a banyan, a sacred fig, or a mango,

2.6.s:
uduṃbaraṃ vā panasaṃ sabhāryāstvaṃ samāviśa /
yasya kākagṛhaṃ niṃbe ārāme vā gṛhepi vā //
2.6.d:
उदुंबरं वा पनसं सभार्यास्त्वं समाविश ।
यस्य काकगृहं निंबे आरामे वा गृहेपि वा ॥
2.6.m: a cluster fig, or a jackfruit tree, enter there together with your wife; / he who has a crow's nest in a neem tree, whether in the garden or in the house,

2.6.s:
daṇḍinī muṇḍinī vāpi sabhāryastvaṃ samāviśa /
ekā dāsī gṛhe yatra trigavaṃ pañcamāhiṣam //
2.6.d:
दण्डिनी मुण्डिनी वापि सभार्यस्त्वं समाविश ।
एका दासी गृहे यत्र त्रिगवं पञ्चमाहिषम् ॥
2.6.m: or a woman carrying a staff or a shaved-headed ascetic woman, enter there together with your wife; / where in a house there is a single female slave, three cows, five buffaloes,

2.6.s:
ṣaḍaśvaṃ saptamātaṅgaṃ sabhāryastvaṃ samāviśa /
yasya kālī gṛhe devī pretarūpā ca ḍākinī //
2.6.d:
षडश्वं सप्तमातङ्गं सभार्यस्त्वं समाविश ।
यस्य काली गृहे देवी प्रेतरूपा च डाकिनी ॥
2.6.m: six horses, and seven elephants, enter there together with your wife; / he in whose house the goddess Kālī is kept, or a ḍākinī in the form of a ghost,

2.6.s:
kṣetrapālethavā yatra sabhāryastvaṃ samāviśa /
bhikṣubiṃbaṃ ca vai yasya gṛhe kṣapaṇakaṃ tathā //
2.6.d:
क्षेत्रपालेथवा यत्र सभार्यस्त्वं समाविश ।
भिक्षुबिंबं च वै यस्य गृहे क्षपणकं तथा ॥
2.6.m: or where there is a guardian of the field, enter there together with your wife; / he in whose house there is an image of a mendicant or a Jain ascetic,

2.6.s:
bauddhaṃ vā biṃbamāsādya tatra pūrṇaṃ samāviśa /
śayanāsanakāleṣu bhojanāṭanavṛttiṣu //
2.6.d:
बौद्धं वा बिंबमासाद्य तत्र पूर्णं समाविश ।
शयनासनकालेषु भोजनाटनवृत्तिषु ॥
2.6.m: or having approached an image of the Buddha, enter there fully. / At the times of lying down, sitting, eating, and roaming about,

2.6.s:
yeṣāṃ vadati no vāṇī nāmāni ca hareḥ sadā /
tadgahaṃ te samākhyātaṃ sabhāryasya niveśitum //
2.6.d:
येषां वदति नो वाणी नामानि च हरेः सदा ।
तद्गहं ते समाख्यातं सभार्यस्य निवेशितुम् ॥
2.6.m: those whose voice never recites the names of Hari— / their house has been declared for you to enter together with your wife.

2.6.s:
pāṣaṇḍācāraniratāḥ śrautasmārtabahiṣkṛtāḥ /
viṣṇubhakti vinirmuktā mahādevavinindakāḥ //
2.6.d:
पाषण्डाचारनिरताः श्रौतस्मार्तबहिष्कृताः ।
विष्णुभक्ति विनिर्मुक्ता महादेवविनिन्दकाः ॥
2.6.m: Those devoted to heretical conduct, excluded from Vedic and traditional codes, / free of devotion to Viṣṇu, revilers of Mahādeva,

2.6.s:
nāstikāśca śaṭhā yatra sabhāryāstvaṃ samāviśa /
sarvasmādadhikatvaṃ ye na vadanti pinākinaḥ //
2.6.d:
नास्तिकाश्च शठा यत्र सभार्यास्त्वं समाविश ।
सर्वस्मादधिकत्वं ये न वदन्ति पिनाकिनः ॥
2.6.m: and where there are atheists and deceivers, enter there together with your wife. / Those who do not proclaim the superiority of Pinākin above all,

2.6.s:
sādhāraṇaṃ smarantyenaṃ sabhāryastvaṃ samāviśa /
brahmā ca bhagavānviṣṇuḥ śakraḥ sarvasureśvaraḥ //
2.6.d:
साधारणं स्मरन्त्येनं सभार्यस्त्वं समाविश ।
ब्रह्मा च भगवान्विष्णुः शक्रः सर्वसुरेश्वरः ॥
2.6.m: and remember him as ordinary, enter there together with your wife. / The evil-minded who do not say,

2.6.s:
rudraprasādajāśceti na vadanti durātmakāḥ /
brahmā ca bhagavānviṣṇuḥ śakraśca sama eva ca //
2.6.d:
रुद्रप्रसादजाश्चेति न वदन्ति दुरात्मकाः ।
ब्रह्मा च भगवान्विष्णुः शक्रश्च सम एव च ॥
2.6.m: “Brahmā, lord Viṣṇu, and Śakra, the ruler of all the gods, / are born from the grace of Rudra,” and who say that Brahmā, lord Viṣṇu,

2.6.s:
vadanti mūḍhāḥ khadyotaṃ bhānuṃ vā mūḍhacetasaḥ /
teṣāṃ gṛhe tathā kṣetra āvāse vā sadānayā //
2.6.d:
वदन्ति मूढाः खद्योतं भानुं वा मूढचेतसः ।
तेषां गृहे तथा क्षेत्र आवासे वा सदानया ॥
2.6.m: and Śakra are merely equal, those fools, foolish-minded, / [comparing] a firefly or the sun—in their house, their field, or their dwelling,

2.6.s:
viśa bhuṅkṣva gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ api pūrṇamananyadhīḥ /
ye 'śranti kevalaṃ mūḍhāḥ pakvamannaṃ vicetasaḥ //
2.6.d:
विश भुङ्क्ष्व गृहं तेषां अपि पूर्णमनन्यधीः ।
ये ऽश्रन्ति केवलं मूढाः पक्वमन्नं विचेतसः ॥
2.6.m: enter always with her, and enjoy their house fully with focused mind. / Those fools who, senseless, eat cooked food alone,

2.6.s:
snānamaṅgalahīnāś ca teṣāṃ tvaṃ gṛham āviśa /
yā nārī śaucavibhraṣṭā dehasaṃskāravarjitā //
2.6.d:
स्नानमङ्गलहीनाश् च तेषां त्वं गृहम् आविश ।
या नारी शौचविभ्रष्टा देहसंस्कारवर्जिता ॥
2.6.m: destitute of bath and auspicious rites—enter their house. / The woman who has fallen from purity, is devoid of bodily purification,

2.6.s:
sarvabhakṣaratā nityaṃ tasyāḥ stāne samāviśa /
malināsyāḥ svayaṃ martyā malināṃbaradhāriṇaḥ //
2.6.d:
सर्वभक्षरता नित्यं तस्याः स्ताने समाविश ।
मलिनास्याः स्वयं मर्त्या मलिनांबरधारिणः ॥
2.6.m: and is constantly devoted to eating everything—enter her abode. / Mortals who themselves have dirty faces, who wear soiled garments,

2.6.s:
maladantā gṛhasthāśca gṛhe teṣāṃ samāviśa /
pādaśaucavinirmuktāḥ saṃdhyākāle ca śāyinaḥ //
2.6.d:
मलदन्ता गृहस्थाश्च गृहे तेषां समाविश ।
पादशौचविनिर्मुक्ताः संध्याकाले च शायिनः ॥
2.6.m: and householders with filthy teeth—enter their house. / Those who neglect washing their feet and sleep at twilight,

2.6.s:
saṃdhyāyāma śrute ye vai gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ samāviśa /
atyāśanaratā martyā atipānaratā narāḥ //
2.6.d:
संध्यायाम श्रुते ये वै गृहं तेषां समाविश ।
अत्याशनरता मर्त्या अतिपानरता नराः ॥
2.6.m: or who [eat or sleep] during twilight when sacred learning [is forbidden]—enter their house. / Mortals devoted to overeating, men devoted to excessive drinking,

2.6.s:
dyūtavādakriyāmūḍhāḥ gṛhe teṣāṃ samāviśa /
brahmasvahāriṇo ye cāyogyāṃścaiva yajanti vā //
2.6.d:
द्यूतवादक्रियामूढाः गृहे तेषां समाविश ।
ब्रह्मस्वहारिणो ये चायोग्यांश्चैव यजन्ति वा ॥
2.6.m: fools given to gambling, disputes, and quarrels—enter their house. / Those who seize the property of Brahmins, or who sacrifice for the unworthy,

2.6.s:
śūdrānnabhojino vāpi gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ samāviśa /
madyapānaratāḥ pāpā māṃsa bhakṣaṇatatparāḥ //
2.6.d:
शूद्रान्नभोजिनो वापि गृहं तेषां समाविश ।
मद्यपानरताः पापा मांस भक्षणतत्पराः ॥
2.6.m: or who eat the food of Śūdras—enter their house. / Sinful people devoted to drinking liquor, intent on eating meat,

2.6.s:
paradāraratā martyā gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ samāviśa /
parvaṇyanarcābhiratā maithune vā divā ratāḥ //
2.6.d:
परदाररता मर्त्या गृहं तेषां समाविश ।
पर्वण्यनर्चाभिरता मैथुने वा दिवा रताः ॥
2.6.m: mortals who pursue the wives of others—enter their house. / Those who delight in not performing rites on festivals, or who engage in intercourse by day,

2.6.s:
saṃdhyāyāṃ maithunaṃ yeṣāṃ gṛhe teṣāṃ samāviśa /
pṛṣṭhato maithunaṃ yeṣāṃ śvānavanmṛgavacca vā //
2.6.d:
संध्यायां मैथुनं येषां गृहे तेषां समाविश ।
पृष्ठतो मैथुनं येषां श्वानवन्मृगवच्च वा ॥
2.6.m: those whose intercourse is at twilight—enter their house. / Those whose intercourse is from behind, like dogs or deer,

2.6.s:
jale vā maithunaṃ kuryātsabhāryastvaṃ samāviśa /
rajasvalāṃ striyaṃ gaccheccāṇḍālīṃ vā narādhamaḥ //
2.6.d:
जले वा मैथुनं कुर्यात्सभार्यस्त्वं समाविश ।
रजस्वलां स्त्रियं गच्छेच्चाण्डालीं वा नराधमः ॥
2.6.m: or if one engages in intercourse in water, enter together with your wife. / If the lowest of men approaches a menstruating woman, a Cāṇḍāla woman,

2.6.s:
kanyāṃ vā gogṛhe vāpi gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ samāviśa /
bahunā kiṃ pralāpena nityakarmabahiṣkṛtāḥ //
2.6.d:
कन्यां वा गोगृहे वापि गृहं तेषां समाविश ।
बहुना किं प्रलापेन नित्यकर्मबहिष्कृताः ॥
2.6.m: an unmarried maiden, or [engages in sex] in a cowshed—enter their house. / What is the use of prolonged babble? Those who are excluded from daily duties

2.6.s:
rudrabhaktivihīnāye gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ samāviśa /
śṛṅgairdivyauṣadhaiḥ kṣudraiḥ śepha ālipya gacchati //
2.6.d:
रुद्रभक्तिविहीनाये गृहं तेषां समाविश ।
शृङ्गैर्दिव्यौषधैः क्षुद्रैः शेफ आलिप्य गच्छति ॥
2.6.m: and are devoid of devotion to Rudra—enter their house. / He who rubs his penis with horns and petty magical herbs and goes,

2.6.s:
bhagadrāvaṃ karotyasmātsabhāryastvaṃ samāviśa /
sūta uvāca
ityuktvā sa muniḥ śrīmān nirmārjya nayane tadā //
2.6.d:
भगद्रावं करोत्यस्मात्सभार्यस्त्वं समाविश ।
सूत उवाच
इत्युक्त्वा स मुनिः श्रीमान् निर्मार्ज्य नयने तदा ॥
2.6.m: and causes the vaginal emission from it—enter there together with your wife.” / Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, that illustrious sage, wiping his eyes then,

2.6.s:
brahmarṣirbrahmasaṃkāśastatraivāntarddhimātanot /
duḥsahaśca tathoktāni stānāni ca samīyivān //
2.6.d:
ब्रह्मर्षिर्ब्रह्मसंकाशस्तत्रैवान्तर्द्धिमातनोत् ।
दुःसहश्च तथोक्तानि स्तानानि च समीयिवान् ॥
2.6.m: the Brahmanical seer, resembling Brahmā, vanished right there. / And Duḥsaha went to the places that had been mentioned [by the sage],

2.6.s:
viśeṣāddevadevasya viṣṇornidāratātmanām /
sabhāryo muniśārdūlaḥ saiṣā jyeṣṭhā iti smṛtā //
2.6.d:
विशेषाद्देवदेवस्य विष्णोर्निदारतात्मनाम् ।
सभार्यो मुनिशार्दूलः सैषा ज्येष्ठा इति स्मृता ॥
2.6.m: especially of those whose minds revile the god of gods, Viṣṇu. / Accompanied by his wife, that tiger among sages—she is known as Jyeṣṭhā—

2.6.s:
duḥsahastāmuvācedaṃ taḍāgāśramamantare /
āsva tvamatra cāhaṃ vai pravekṣyāmi rasātalam //
2.6.d:
दुःसहस्तामुवाचेदं तडागाश्रममन्तरे ।
आस्व त्वमत्र चाहं वै प्रवेक्ष्यामि रसातलम् ॥
2.6.m: Duḥsaha spoke these words to her midway between the pond and the hermitage: / “Remain here, and I shall enter the netherworld.

2.6.s:
āvayoḥ sthānamālokya nivāsārthaṃ tataḥ punaḥ /
āgamiṣyāmi te pārśvamityuktā tamuvāca sā //
2.6.d:
आवयोः स्थानमालोक्य निवासार्थं ततः पुनः ।
आगमिष्यामि ते पार्श्वमित्युक्ता तमुवाच सा ॥
2.6.m: Having looked for a place for our residence, I will come back / to your side again.” When she was told this, she said to him:

2.6.s:
kimaśrāmi mahābhāga ko me dāsyati vai balim /
ityuktastāṃ muniḥ prāha yāḥ striyastvāṃ yajanti vai //
2.6.d:
किमश्रामि महाभाग को मे दास्यति वै बलिम् ।
इत्युक्तस्तां मुनिः प्राह याः स्त्रियस्त्वां यजन्ति वै ॥
2.6.m: “What shall I eat, O highly fortunate one? Who will give me an offering?” / Addressed thus, the sage said to her: “Those women who sacrifice to you

2.6.s:
balibhiḥ puṣpadhūpaiśca na tāsāṃ ca gṛhaṃ viśa /
ityuktvā tvāviśattatra pātālaṃ bilayogataḥ //
2.6.d:
बलिभिः पुष्पधूपैश्च न तासां च गृहं विश ।
इत्युक्त्वा त्वाविशत्तत्र पातालं बिलयोगतः ॥
2.6.m: with offerings, flowers, and incense—do not enter their house.” / Having spoken thus, he entered the subterranean realm through a hole.

2.6.s:
adyāpi ca vinirmagno muniḥ sa jalasaṃstare /
grāmaparvatabāhyeṣu nityamāste 'śubhā punaḥ //
2.6.d:
अद्यापि च विनिर्मग्नो मुनिः स जलसंस्तरे ।
ग्रामपर्वतबाह्येषु नित्यमास्ते ऽशुभा पुनः ॥
2.6.m: Even today that sage remains submerged in a bed of water; / and that inauspicious woman constantly stays outside villages and mountains.

2.6.s:
prasaṃgāddevandeveśo viṣṇustribhuvaneśvaraḥ /
lakṣmyā dṛṣṭastayā lakṣmīḥ sā tamāha janārdanam //
2.6.d:
प्रसंगाद्देवन्देवेशो विष्णुस्त्रिभुवनेश्वरः ।
लक्ष्म्या दृष्टस्तया लक्ष्मीः सा तमाह जनार्दनम् ॥
2.6.m: In the course of time, Viṣṇu, the lord of gods, the lord of the three worlds, / was seen by Lakṣmī. That Lakṣmī said to Janārdana:

2.6.s:
bhartā gato mahābāho bilaṃ tyaktvā sa māṃ prabho /
anāthāhaṃ jagannātha vṛttiṃ dehi namostu te //
2.6.d:
भर्ता गतो महाबाहो बिलं त्यक्त्वा स मां प्रभो ।
अनाथाहं जगन्नाथ वृत्तिं देहि नमोस्तु ते ॥
2.6.m: “O mighty-armed lord, my husband has gone into a hole, abandoning me. / I am helpless, O Lord of the Universe; grant me a livelihood! Homage be to you!”

2.6.s:
sūta uvāca
ityukto bhagavānviṣṇuḥ prahasyāha janārdanaḥ /
jyeṣṭhāmalakṣmīṃ deveśo mādhavo madhusūdanaḥ //
2.6.d:
सूत उवाच
इत्युक्तो भगवान्विष्णुः प्रहस्याह जनार्दनः ।
ज्येष्ठामलक्ष्मीं देवेशो माधवो मधुसूदनः ॥
2.6.m: Sūta said: / Addressed thus, lord Viṣṇu, Janārdana, laughing gently, / the lord of the gods, Mādhava, Madhusūdana, spoke to Jyeṣṭhā Alakṣmī.

2.6.s:
śrīviṣṇuruvāca
ye rudramanaghaṃ śarvaṃ śaṅkaraṃ nīlalohitam /
aṃbāṃ haimavatīṃ vāpi janitrīṃ jagatāmapi //
2.6.d:
श्रीविष्णुरुवाच
ये रुद्रमनघं शर्वं शङ्करं नीललोहितम् ।
अंबां हैमवतीं वापि जनित्रीं जगतामपि ॥
2.6.m: Lord Viṣṇu said: / “Those who revile sinless Rudra, Śarva, Śaṅkara, Nīlalohita, / or Mother Haimavatī, the progenitor of the worlds,

2.6.s:
madbhaktānnindayantyatra teṣāṃ vittaṃ tavaiva hi /
yepi caiva mahādevaṃ vinindyaiva yajanti mām //
2.6.d:
मद्भक्तान्निन्दयन्त्यत्र तेषां वित्तं तवैव हि ।
येपि चैव महादेवं विनिन्द्यैव यजन्ति माम् ॥
2.6.m: or who revile my devotees here—their wealth is yours alone. / And also those fools who revile Mahādeva and worship me,

2.6.s:
mūḍhā hyabhāgyā madbhaktā api teṣāṃ dhanaṃ tava /
yasyājñayā hyahaṃ brahmā prasādādvartate sadā //
2.6.d:
मूढा ह्यभाग्या मद्भक्ता अपि तेषां धनं तव ।
यस्याज्ञया ह्यहं ब्रह्मा प्रसादाद्वर्तते सदा ॥
2.6.m: the unfortunate ones, even if they are my devotees, their wealth is yours. / By whose command Brahmā and I exist always through his grace,

2.6.s:
ye yajanti vinindyaiva mama vidveṣakārakāḥ /
madbhaktā naiva te bhaktā iva vartanti durmadāḥ //
2.6.d:
ये यजन्ति विनिन्द्यैव मम विद्वेषकारकाः ।
मद्भक्ता नैव ते भक्ता इव वर्तन्ति दुर्मदाः ॥
2.6.m: those who worship [me] while reviling [him] cause hatred toward me; / they are not my devotees, but live as if they were devotees, arrogant with delusion.

2.6.s:
teṣāṃ gṛhaṃ dhanaṃ kṣetramiṣṭāpūrtaṃ tavaiva hi /
sūta uvāca
ityuktvā tāṃ parityajya lakṣmyālakṣmīṃ janārdanaḥ //
2.6.d:
तेषां गृहं धनं क्षेत्रमिष्टापूर्तं तवैव हि ।
सूत उवाच
इत्युक्त्वा तां परित्यज्य लक्ष्म्यालक्ष्मीं जनार्दनः ॥
2.6.m: Their house, wealth, field, and sacrifices and charitable works are yours alone.” / Sūta said: / Having spoken thus and abandoned that Alakṣmī along with Lakṣmī, Janārdana

2.6.s:
jajāpa bhagavanrudramalakṣmīkṣayasiddhaye /
tasmātpradeyastasyai ca balirnityaṃmunīśvarāḥ //
2.6.d:
जजाप भगवन्रुद्रमलक्ष्मीक्षयसिद्धये ।
तस्मात्प्रदेयस्तस्यै च बलिर्नित्यंमुनीश्वराः ॥
2.6.m: chanted [the name of] lord Rudra for the purpose of destroying Alakṣmī. / Therefore an offering must be given to her daily, O foremost among sages,

2.6.s:
viṣṇubhaktairna saṃdehaḥ sarvayatnena sarvadā /
aṅganābhiḥ sadā pūjyā balibhirvividhairdvijāḥ //
2.6.d:
विष्णुभक्तैर्न संदेहः सर्वयत्नेन सर्वदा ।
अङ्गनाभिः सदा पूज्या बलिभिर्विविधैर्द्विजाः ॥
2.6.m: by the devotees of Viṣṇu, without doubt, with every effort, at all times; / she should always be worshipped by women with various offerings, O twice-born.

2.6.s:
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi śrāvayedvā dvijottamān /
alakṣmīvṛttamanagho lakṣmīvāllaṃbhate gatim //
iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge alakṣmīvṛttaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭhe 'dhyāyaḥ
2.6.d:
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्वापि श्रावयेद्वा द्विजोत्तमान् ।
अलक्ष्मीवृत्तमनघो लक्ष्मीवाल्लंभते गतिम् ॥
इति श्रीलिङ्गमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे अलक्ष्मीवृत्तं नाम षष्ठे ऽध्यायः
2.6.m:
He who reads, listens to, or recites to the best of the twice-born / this account of Alakṣmī, becomes sinless, endowed with fortune, and attains the goal.

Thus ends the sixth chapter named 'The Story of Alakṣmī' in the Uttarabhāga of the glorious Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa.

2.7.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
kiñjapānmucyate jantuḥ sarvalokabhayādibhiḥ /
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim //
2.7.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
किञ्जपान्मुच्यते जन्तुः सर्वलोकभयादिभिः ।
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः प्राप्नोति परमां गतिम् ॥
2.7.m:
The sages said:
By chanting what is a living being freed from fears and the like in all worlds?
Freed from all sins, [how] does he attain the highest goal?

2.7.s:
alakṣmīṃvātha saṃtyajya gamiṣyati japena vai /
lakṣmīvāso bhavenmartyaḥ sūta vaktumihārhasi //
2.7.d:
अलक्ष्मींवाथ संत्यज्य गमिष्यति जपेन वै ।
लक्ष्मीवासो भवेन्मर्त्यः सूत वक्तुमिहार्हसि ॥
2.7.m:
Or by casting off Alakṣmī, will he indeed depart through chanting?
A mortal would become the abode of fortune (Lakṣmī); O Sūta, you ought to speak of this here.

2.7.s:
sūta uvāca
purā pitāmahenoktaṃ vasiṣṭhāya mahātmane /
vakṣye saṃkṣepataḥ sarvaṃ sarvalokahitāya vai //
2.7.d:
सूत उवाच
पुरा पितामहेनोक्तं वसिष्ठाय महात्मने ।
वक्ष्ये संक्षेपतः सर्वं सर्वलोकहिताय वै ॥
2.7.m:
Sūta said:
What was told of old by Pitāmaha to high-souled Vasiṣṭha,
all that I will tell in brief, indeed for the welfare of all worlds.

2.7.s:
śṛṇvantu vacanaṃ sarve praṇipatya janārdanam /
devadevamajaṃ viṣṇuṃ kṛṣṇamacyutamavyayam //
2.7.d:
शृण्वन्तु वचनं सर्वे प्रणिपत्य जनार्दनम् ।
देवदेवमजं विष्णुं कृष्णमच्युतमव्ययम् ॥
2.7.m:
Let all hear the words, having bowed down to Janārdana,
the God of gods, unborn Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa, Acyuta, the imperishable,

2.7.s:
sarvapāpaharaṃ śuddhaṃ mokṣadaṃ brahmavādinam /
manasākarmaṇā vācā yo vidvānpuṇyakarmakṛt //
2.7.d:
सर्वपापहरं शुद्धं मोक्षदं ब्रह्मवादिनम् ।
मनसाकर्मणा वाचा यो विद्वान्पुण्यकर्मकृत् ॥
2.7.m:
the dispeller of all sins, pure, bestower of liberation, teacher of the Veda.
Whatever wise person who performs meritorious deeds, by mind, action, and speech,

2.7.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ japennityaṃ praṇamya puruṣottamam /
svapannārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ gacchannārāyaṇaṃ tathā //
2.7.d:
नारायणं जपेन्नित्यं प्रणम्य पुरुषोत्तमम् ।
स्वपन्नारायणं देवं गच्छन्नारायणं तथा ॥
2.7.m:
should constantly chant 'Nārāyaṇa', having bowed to Puruṣottama;
while sleeping, the divine Nārāyaṇa; likewise while walking, Nārāyaṇa;

2.7.s:
bhuñjannārāyaṇaṃ viprāstiṣṭhañjāgratsanātanam /
unmiṣannimiṣanvāpi namo nārāyaṇeti vai //
2.7.d:
भुञ्जन्नारायणं विप्रास्तिष्ठञ्जाग्रत्सनातनम् ।
उन्मिषन्निमिषन्वापि नमो नारायणेति वै ॥
2.7.m:
while eating, Nārāyaṇa, O brahmins; standing, waking, the eternal one;
or while opening or closing the eyes, indeed [saying] 'Homage to Nārāyaṇa'—

2.7.s:
bhojyaṃ peyaṃ ca lehyaṃ ca namo nārāyaṇeti ca /
abhimantrya spṛśanbhuṅkte sa yāti paramāṃ gatim //
2.7.d:
भोज्यं पेयं च लेह्यं च नमो नारायणेति च ।
अभिमन्त्र्य स्पृशन्भुङ्क्ते स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
2.7.m:
Touching food, drink, and things to be licked, and having consecrated [them] with 'Homage to Nārāyaṇa',
he who eats goes to the highest goal.

2.7.s:
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ prāpnoti ca satāṃ gatim /
alakṣmīśca mayā proktā patnī yā duḥsahasya ca //
2.7.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः प्राप्नोति च सतां गतिम् ।
अलक्ष्मीश्च मया प्रोक्ता पत्नी या दुःसहस्य च ॥
2.7.m:
Freed from all sins, he attains the destination of the virtuous.
And Alakṣmī, whom I described as the wife of Duḥsaha,

2.7.s:
nārāyaṇapadaṃ śrutvā gacchatyeva na saṃśayaḥ /
yā lakṣmīrdevadevasya hareḥ kṛṣṇasya vallabhā //
2.7.d:
नारायणपदं श्रुत्वा गच्छत्येव न संशयः ।
या लक्ष्मीर्देवदेवस्य हरेः कृष्णस्य वल्लभा ॥
2.7.m:
upon hearing the word 'Nārāyaṇa', departs indeed, no doubt.
That Lakṣmī who is beloved of the God of gods, Hari, Kṛṣṇa,

2.7.s:
gṛhe kṣetre tathāvāse tanauvasati suvratāḥ /
āloḍya sarvaśāstrāṇi vicārya ca punaḥ punaḥ //
2.7.d:
गृहे क्षेत्रे तथावासे तनौवसति सुव्रताः ।
आलोड्य सर्वशास्त्राणि विचार्य च पुनः पुनः ॥
2.7.m:
resides in the house, field, abode, and body [of such a person], O you of good vows.
Having churned all the scriptures and having reflected again and again,

2.7.s:
itamekaṃ suniṣpannaṃ dhyeyo nārāyaṇaḥ sadā /
kiṃ tasya bahubhirmantraiḥ kiṃ tasya bahubhirvrataiḥ //
2.7.d:
इतमेकं सुनिष्पन्नं ध्येयो नारायणः सदा ।
किं तस्य बहुभिर्मन्त्रैः किं तस्य बहुभिर्व्रतैः ॥
2.7.m:
this single conclusion is firmly reached: Nārāyaṇa is to be meditated upon always.
What is the use of many mantras to him? What is the use of many vows to him?

2.7.s:
namo nārāyaṇāyeti mantraḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ /
tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu namo nārāyaṇeti ca //
2.7.d:
नमो नारायणायेति मन्त्रः सर्वार्थसाधकः ।
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु नमो नारायणेति च ॥
2.7.m:
The mantra 'Homage to Nārāyaṇa' accomplishes all goals.
Therefore, at all times, 'Homage to Nārāyaṇa'—

2.7.s:
japetsa yāti viprendrā viṣṇulokaṃ sabāndhavaḥ /
anyacca devadevasya śṛṇvantu munisattamāḥ //
2.7.d:
जपेत्स याति विप्रेन्द्रा विष्णुलोकं सबान्धवः ।
अन्यच्च देवदेवस्य शृण्वन्तु मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
2.7.m:
he who chants this, O best of brahmins, goes to the world of Viṣṇu with his kinsmen.
Moreover, hear of another [mantra] of the God of gods, O best of sages.

2.7.s:
mantro mayā purābhyastaḥ sarvavedārthasādhakaḥ /
dvādaśākṣarasaṃyukto dvādaśātmā purātanaḥ //
2.7.d:
मन्त्रो मया पुराभ्यस्तः सर्ववेदार्थसाधकः ।
द्वादशाक्षरसंयुक्तो द्वादशात्मा पुरातनः ॥
2.7.m:
A mantra was practiced by me of old, accomplishing the meaning of all Vedas,
endowed with twelve syllables, twelve-formed, ancient.

2.7.s:
tasyaiveha ca māhātmyaṃ saṃkṣepātpravadāmi vaḥ /
kaściddvijo mahāprājñastapastaptvā kathañcana //
2.7.d:
तस्यैवेह च माहात्म्यं संक्षेपात्प्रवदामि वः ।
कश्चिद्द्विजो महाप्राज्ञस्तपस्तप्त्वा कथञ्चन ॥
2.7.m:
Its majesty alone I shall proclaim to you here in brief.
A certain brahmin of great wisdom, having performed austerities somehow,

2.7.s:
putramekaṃ tayotpādya saṃskāraiśca yathākramam /
yojayitvā yatākālaṃ kṛtopanayanaṃ punaḥ //
2.7.d:
पुत्रमेकं तयोत्पाद्य संस्कारैश्च यथाक्रमम् ।
योजयित्वा यताकालं कृतोपनयनं पुनः ॥
2.7.m:
and having begotten one son by her, and by rites in proper order
having joined him, having performed the sacred thread ceremony again when the time came,

2.7.s:
adhyāpayāmāsa tadā sa ca novāca kiñcana /
na jihvā spandate tasya duḥkhito 'bhūddvijottamaḥ //
2.7.d:
अध्यापयामास तदा स च नोवाच किञ्चन ।
न जिह्वा स्पन्दते तस्य दुःखितो ऽभूद्द्विजोत्तमः ॥
2.7.m:
instructed him then; and he spoke nothing at all.
His tongue did not move; the best of brahmins became sorrowful.

2.7.s:
vāsudeveti niyatamaitareyo vadatyasau /
pitā tasya tathā cānyāṃ pariṇīya yathāvidhi //
2.7.d:
वासुदेवेति नियतमैतरेयो वदत्यसौ ।
पिता तस्य तथा चान्यां परिणीय यथाविधि ॥
2.7.m:
This son of Itarā (Aitareya) constantly said 'Vāsudeva'.
Then his father, having married another woman according to the rule,

2.7.s:
putrānutpādayāmāsa tathaiva vidhipūrvakam /
vedānadhītya saṃpannā babhūvuḥ sarvasaṃmatāḥ //
2.7.d:
पुत्रानुत्पादयामास तथैव विधिपूर्वकम् ।
वेदानधीत्य संपन्ना बभूवुः सर्वसंमताः ॥
2.7.m:
begot sons likewise according to the rule.
Having studied the Vedas, they became accomplished and approved by all.

2.7.s:
aitareyasya sā mātā duḥkhitā śokamūrcchitā /
uvāca putrāḥ saṃpannā vedavedāṅgapāragāḥ //
2.7.d:
ऐतरेयस्य सा माता दुःखिता शोकमूर्च्छिता ।
उवाच पुत्राः संपन्ना वेदवेदाङ्गपारगाः ॥
2.7.m:
That mother of Aitareya, sorrowful and overwhelmed with grief,
said: 'The sons [of the other wife] are accomplished, masters of the Vedas and auxiliary sciences;

2.7.s:
brāhmaṇaiḥ pūjyamānā vai modayanti ca mātaram /
mama tvaṃ bhāgyahīnāyāḥ putro jāto nirākṛtiḥ //
2.7.d:
ब्राह्मणैः पूज्यमाना वै मोदयन्ति च मातरम् ।
मम त्वं भाग्यहीनायाः पुत्रो जातो निराकृतिः ॥
2.7.m:
being honoured by brahmins, they delight their mother.
To me, unfortunate, you were born as a son deformed / useless.

2.7.s:
mamātra nidhanaṃ śreyo na kathañcana jīvitam /
ityuktaḥ sa ca nirgamya yajñavāṭaṃ jagāma vai //
2.7.d:
ममात्र निधनं श्रेयो न कथञ्चन जीवितम् ।
इत्युक्तः स च निर्गम्य यज्ञवाटं जगाम वै ॥
2.7.m:
Death in this situation is better for me, not life in any way.'
Addressed thus, he departed and indeed went to the sacrificial enclosure.

2.7.s:
tasminyāte dvijānāṃ tu na mantrāḥ pratipedire /
aitareye sthitetatra brāhmaṇā mohitāstadā //
2.7.d:
तस्मिन्याते द्विजानां तु न मन्त्राः प्रतिपेदिरे ।
ऐतरेये स्थितेतत्र ब्राह्मणा मोहितास्तदा ॥
2.7.m:
When he had gone, the mantras of the brahmins did not manifest.
While Aitareya stood there, the brahmins were then bewildered.

2.7.s:
tato vāṇī samudbhūtā vāsudeveti kīrtanāt /
aitareyasya te viprāḥ praṇipatya yatātatham //
2.7.d:
ततो वाणी समुद्भूता वासुदेवेति कीर्तनात् ।
ऐतरेयस्य ते विप्राः प्रणिपत्य यतातथम् ॥
2.7.m:
Then a voice arose from the chanting of 'Vāsudeva'.
Having bowed down to Aitareya just as it was, those brahmins

2.7.s:
pūjāṃ cakrustato yajñaṃ svayameva samāgatam /
tataḥ samāpya taṃ yajñamaitareyo dhanādibhiḥ //
2.7.d:
पूजां चक्रुस्ततो यज्ञं स्वयमेव समागतम् ।
ततः समाप्य तं यज्ञमैतरेयो धनादिभिः ॥
2.7.m:
performed worship; thereupon the sacrifice manifested of its own accord.
Then, having completed that sacrifice with wealth and other things, Aitareya,

2.7.s:
sarvavedānsadasyāha sa ṣaḍaṅgān samāhitāḥ /
tuṣṭuvuśca tathā viprā brahmādyāśca tathā dvijāḥ //
2.7.d:
सर्ववेदान्सदस्याह स षडङ्गान् समाहिताः ।
तुष्टुवुश्च तथा विप्रा ब्रह्माद्याश्च तथा द्विजाः ॥
2.7.m:
composed, recited all the Vedas with their six limbs to the assembly;
and so the brahmins and the priests headed by Brahmā praised him.

2.7.s:
sasarjuḥ puṣpavarṣāṇi khecarāḥ siddhacāraṇāḥ /
evaṃ samāpya vai yajñamaitareyo dvijottamāḥ //
2.7.d:
ससर्जुः पुष्पवर्षाणि खेचराः सिद्धचारणाः ।
एवं समाप्य वै यज्ञमैतरेयो द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
2.7.m:
Sky-dwellers, Siddhas, and Cāraṇas showered rains of flowers.
Having completed the sacrifice in this way, O best of brahmins, Aitareya,

2.7.s:
mātaraṃ pūjayitvā tu viṣṇoḥ sthānaṃ jagāma ha /
etadvai kathitaṃ sarvaṃ dvādaśākṣaravaibhavam //
2.7.d:
मातरं पूजयित्वा तु विष्णोः स्थानं जगाम ह ।
एतद्वै कथितं सर्वं द्वादशाक्षरवैभवम् ॥
2.7.m:
having honoured his mother, went to the abode of Viṣṇu.
All this glory of the twelve-syllable [mantra] has indeed been told.

2.7.s:
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ nityaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam /
japedyaḥ puruṣo nityaṃ dvādaśākṣaramavyayam //
2.7.d:
पठतां शृण्वतां नित्यं महापातकनाशनम् ।
जपेद्यः पुरुषो नित्यं द्वादशाक्षरमव्ययम् ॥
2.7.m:
For those who read and listen, it is always the destroyer of great sins.
The man who constantly chants the imperishable twelve-syllable [mantra],

2.7.s:
sa yāti divyamatulaṃ viṣṇostatparamaṃ padam /
api pāpasamācāro dvādaśākṣaratatparaḥ //
2.7.d:
स याति दिव्यमतुलं विष्णोस्तत्परमं पदम् ।
अपि पापसमाचारो द्वादशाक्षरतत्परः ॥
2.7.m:
goes to that divine, peerless, highest abode of Viṣṇu.
Even one of sinful conduct, intent upon the twelve-syllable [mantra],

2.7.s:
prāpnoti paramaṃ sthānaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā /
kiṃ punarye svadharmasthā vāsudevaparāyaṇāḥ //
2.7.d:
प्राप्नोति परमं स्थानं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।
किं पुनर्ये स्वधर्मस्था वासुदेवपरायणाः ॥
2.7.m:
attains the highest abode; no doubt should be entertained in this matter.
How much more then those who stand in their own duty, devoted to Vāsudeva!

2.7.s:
divyaṃ sthānaṃ mahātmānaḥ prāpnuvantīti suvratāḥ //
iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge dvādaśākṣarapraśaṃsānāma saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.7.d:
दिव्यं स्थानं महात्मानः प्राप्नुवन्तीति सुव्रताः ॥
इति श्रीलिङ्गमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे द्वादशाक्षरप्रशंसानाम सप्तमो ऽध्यायः
2.7.m:
The great-souled ones attain the divine abode, O you of good vows.

Thus ends the seventh chapter named 'Praise of the Twelve-Syllable Mantra' in the Uttarabhāga of the glorious Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa.

2.8.s:
suta uvāca
aṣṭākṣaro dvijaśreṣṭhā namo nārāyaṇeti ca /
dvādaśākṣaramantraśca paramaḥ paramātmanaḥ //
2.8.d:
सुत उवाच
अष्टाक्षरो द्विजश्रेष्ठा नमो नारायणेति च ।
द्वादशाक्षरमन्त्रश्च परमः परमात्मनः ॥

2.8.s:
mantra ṣaḍakṣaro viprāḥ sarvavedārthasaṃcayaḥ /
yaścoṃnamaḥ śivāyeti mantraḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ //
2.8.d:
मन्त्र षडक्षरो विप्राः सर्ववेदार्थसंचयः ।
यश्चोंनमः शिवायेति मन्त्रः सर्वार्थसाधकः ॥
2.8.m:
The six-syllable mantra, O brahmins, is the aggregate of all Vedic meaning;
and the mantra that is 'Oṃ, homage to Śiva' accomplishes all goals.

2.8.s:
tathā śivatarāyeti divyaḥ pañcākṣaraḥ śubhaḥ /
mayaskarāya cetyevaṃ namaste śaṅkarāya ca //
2.8.d:
तथा शिवतरायेति दिव्यः पञ्चाक्षरः शुभः ।
मयस्कराय चेत्येवं नमस्ते शङ्कराय च ॥
2.8.m:
Likewise, 'to the most auspicious one' is divine, five-syllabled, auspicious;
and 'to the maker of bliss', and 'homage to you, Śaṅkara'—

2.8.s:
saptākṣaroyaṃ rudrasya pradhānapuruṣasya vai /
brahmā ca bhagavānviṣṇuḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ //
2.8.d:
सप्ताक्षरोयं रुद्रस्य प्रधानपुरुषस्य वै ।
ब्रह्मा च भगवान्विष्णुः सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः ॥
2.8.m:
this seven-syllable [mantra] belongs to Rudra, the Pradhāna and Puruṣa.
Brahmā, the Lord Viṣṇu, and all the gods accompanied by Indra,

2.8.s:
mantrairetairdvijaśreṣṭhā munayaśca yajanti tam /
śaṅkaraṃ devadevaśaṃ mayaskaramajodbhavam //
2.8.d:
मन्त्रैरेतैर्द्विजश्रेष्ठा मुनयश्च यजन्ति तम् ।
शङ्करं देवदेवशं मयस्करमजोद्भवम् ॥
2.8.m:
and the sages, O best of brahmins, worship him with these mantras:
Śaṅkara, the lord of the gods, the maker of bliss, born of the unborn,

2.8.s:
śivaṃ ca śaṅkaraṃ rudraṃ devadevamumāpatim /
prāhurnamaḥ śivāyoti namaste śaṅkarāya ca //
2.8.d:
शिवं च शङ्करं रुद्रं देवदेवमुमापतिम् ।
प्राहुर्नमः शिवायोति नमस्ते शङ्कराय च ॥
2.8.m:
Śiva, Śaṅkara, Rudra, the God of gods, husband of Umā.
They recite: 'Homage to Śiva', and 'Homage to you, Śaṅkara,

2.8.s:
mayaskarāya rudrāya tathā śivatarāya ca /
japtvā mucyeta vai vipro brahmahatyādibhiḥ kṣaṇāt //
2.8.d:
मयस्कराय रुद्राय तथा शिवतराय च ।
जप्त्वा मुच्येत वै विप्रो ब्रह्महत्यादिभिः क्षणात् ॥
2.8.m:
to the maker of bliss, to Rudra, and to the most auspicious one.'
Having chanted [this], a brahmin is instantly freed from the murder of a brahmin and other [sins].

2.8.s:
purā kaściddvijaḥ śakto dhundhumūka iti śrutaḥ /
āsīttṛtīye tretāyāmāvartte ca manoḥ prabhoḥ //
2.8.d:
पुरा कश्चिद्द्विजः शक्तो धुन्धुमूक इति श्रुतः ।
आसीत्तृतीये त्रेतायामावर्त्ते च मनोः प्रभोः ॥
2.8.m:
Anciently, a certain capable brahmin was renowned as Dhundhumūka.
He existed in the third Treta in the cycle of the lord Manu,

2.8.s:
meghavāhanakalpe vai brahmaṇaḥ paramātmanaḥ /
megho bhūtvā mahādevaṃ kṛttivāsasamīśvaram //
2.8.d:
मेघवाहनकल्पे वै ब्रह्मणः परमात्मनः ।
मेघो भूत्वा महादेवं कृत्तिवाससमीश्वरम् ॥
2.8.m:
in the Meghavāhana kalpa of Brahmā, the Supreme Self.
Having become a cloud, [carrying] Mahādeva, the lord clad in hide,

2.8.s:
bahumānena vai rudraṃ devadevo janārdanaḥ /
khinno 'tibhārādrudrasya niḥśvāsocchvāsavarjitaḥ //
2.8.d:
बहुमानेन वै रुद्रं देवदेवो जनार्दनः ।
खिन्नो ऽतिभाराद्रुद्रस्य निःश्वासोच्छ्वासवर्जितः ॥
2.8.m:
with great respect indeed to Rudra, the God of gods Janārdana,
exhausted by the extreme weight of Rudra, deprived of exhalation and inhalation,

2.8.s:
vijñāpya śitikaṇṭhāya tapaścakreṃbujekṣaṇaḥ /
tapasā paramaiśvaryaṃ balaṃ caiva tathādbhutam //
2.8.d:
विज्ञाप्य शितिकण्ठाय तपश्चक्रेंबुजेक्षणः ।
तपसा परमैश्वर्यं बलं चैव तथाद्भुतम् ॥
2.8.m:
having made an appeal to the blue-throated one, the lotus-eyed [Viṣṇu] performed austerity.
Through austerity, supreme sovereignty and also wonderful strength

2.8.s:
labdhavānparameśānācchaṅkarātparamātmanaḥ /
tasmātkalpastadā cāsīnmeghavāhanasaṃjñayā //
2.8.d:
लब्धवान्परमेशानाच्छङ्करात्परमात्मनः ।
तस्मात्कल्पस्तदा चासीन्मेघवाहनसंज्ञया ॥
2.8.m:
he obtained from the Supreme Lord, Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self.
Therefore, the kalpa then became known by the name Meghavāhana.

2.8.s:
tasminkalpe muneḥ śāpaddhundhumūkasamudbhavaḥ /
dhundhumūkātmajastena durātmā ca babhūva saḥ //
2.8.d:
तस्मिन्कल्पे मुनेः शापद्धुन्धुमूकसमुद्भवः ।
धुन्धुमूकात्मजस्तेन दुरात्मा च बभूव सः ॥
2.8.m:
In that kalpa, due to a sage's curse, there was the birth of Dhundhumūka;
because of that, the son of Dhundhumūka became evil-minded.

2.8.s:
dhundhumūkaḥ purāsakto bhāryayā saha mohitaḥ /
tasyāṃ vai sthāpito garbhaḥ kāmāsaktena cetasā //
2.8.d:
धुन्धुमूकः पुरासक्तो भार्यया सह मोहितः ।
तस्यां वै स्थापितो गर्भः कामासक्तेन चेतसा ॥
2.8.m:
Dhundhumūka was previously attached, deluded together with his wife;
in her, a womb was indeed placed by a mind attached to desire.

2.8.s:
amāvāsyāmahanyeva muhūrte rudradaivate /
antarvatnī tadā bhāryā muktā tena yathāsukham //
2.8.d:
अमावास्यामहन्येव मुहूर्ते रुद्रदैवते ।
अन्तर्वत्नी तदा भार्या मुक्ता तेन यथासुखम् ॥
2.8.m: On the very day of the new moon, in the muhūrta sacred to Rudra, / his pregnant wife was then released [from labor] happily.

2.8.s:
asūta sā ca tanayaṃ viśalyākhyā prayatnataḥ /
rudre muhurte mandena vīkṣite munisattamāḥ //
2.8.d:
असूत सा च तनयं विशल्याख्या प्रयत्नतः ।
रुद्रे मुहुर्ते मन्देन वीक्षिते मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
2.8.m: She, named Viśalyā, with great effort brought forth a son, / in the muhūrta of Rudra, aspected by Saturn, O best of sages.

2.8.s:
mātuḥ pitustathāriṣṭaṃ sa saṃjātastathātmanaḥ /
ṛṣī tamūcaturviprā dhundhumūkaṃ mithastadā //
2.8.d:
मातुः पितुस्तथारिष्टं स संजातस्तथात्मनः ।
ऋषी तमूचतुर्विप्रा धुन्धुमूकं मिथस्तदा ॥
2.8.m: A calamity arose for both his mother and father, and likewise for himself. / O brāhmaṇas, two ṛṣis then said to Dhundhumūka mutually:

2.8.s:
mitrāvaruṇānāmanau duṣputra iti sattamau /
vasiṣṭhaḥ prāha nīco 'pi prabhāvādvai bṛhaspateḥ //
2.8.d:
मित्रावरुणानामनौ दुष्पुत्र इति सत्तमौ ।
वसिष्ठः प्राह नीचो ऽपि प्रभावाद्वै बृहस्पतेः ॥
2.8.m: The two best [sages], named Mitrāvaruṇa, said, “He is a wicked son.” / Vasiṣṭha said: “Even though he is base, by the power of Bṛhaspati,

2.8.s:
putrastavāsau durbuddhirapi mucyati kilbiṣāt /
duḥkhito dhundhumūko 'sau dṛṣṭvā putram avasthitam //
2.8.d:
पुत्रस्तवासौ दुर्बुद्धिरपि मुच्यति किल्बिषात् ।
दुःखितो धुन्धुमूको ऽसौ दृष्ट्वा पुत्रम् अवस्थितम् ॥
2.8.m: this foolish son of yours will be freed from sin.” / That Dhundhumūka, aggrieved upon seeing his son situated [thus],

2.8.s:
jātakarmādikaṃ kṛtvā vidhivatsvayameva ca /
adhyāpayāmāsa ca taṃ vidhinaiva dvijottamāḥ //
2.8.d:
जातकर्मादिकं कृत्वा विधिवत्स्वयमेव च ।
अध्यापयामास च तं विधिनैव द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
2.8.m: himself performed the birth-rites and other ceremonies according to rule, / and also had him instructed according to the proper precept, O best of the twice-born.

2.8.s:
tenādhīnaṃ yathānyāyaṃ dhaindhumūkena suvratāḥ /
kṛtodvāhastadā gatvā guruśuśruṣaṇe rataḥ //
2.8.d:
तेनाधीनं यथान्यायं धैन्धुमूकेन सुव्रताः ।
कृतोद्वाहस्तदा गत्वा गुरुशुश्रुषणे रतः ॥
2.8.m: That son of Dhundhumūka studied properly, O you of noble vows; / having married, he went and devoted himself to the service of his guru.

2.8.s:
anenaiva muniśreṣṭhā dhaindhumūkena durmadāt /
bhuktvānyāṃ vṛṣalīṃ dṛṣṭvā svabhāryāvāddivāniśam //
2.8.d:
अनेनैव मुनिश्रेष्ठा धैन्धुमूकेन दुर्मदात् ।
भुक्त्वान्यां वृषलीं दृष्ट्वा स्वभार्यावाद्दिवानिशम् ॥
2.8.m: O best of sages, out of sheer infatuation this son of Dhundhumūka, / having seen another outcaste woman, enjoyed her day and night like his own wife.

2.8.s:
ekaśayyāsanagato dhaindhumūko dvijādhamaḥ /
tathā cacāra durbuddhistyaktvā dharmagatiṃ parām //
2.8.d:
एकशय्यासनगतो धैन्धुमूको द्विजाधमः ।
तथा चचार दुर्बुद्धिस्त्यक्त्वा धर्मगतिं पराम् ॥
2.8.m: Sharing one bed and seat, that basest of the twice-born, the son of Dhundhumūka, / that fool, behaved in that manner, having abandoned the supreme path of dharma.

2.8.s:
mādhvī pītā tayā sārdhaṃ tena rāgavivṛddhaye /
kenāpi kāraṇenaiva tāmuddisya dvijottamāḥ //
2.8.d:
माध्वी पीता तया सार्धं तेन रागविवृद्धये ।
केनापि कारणेनैव तामुद्दिस्य द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
2.8.m: Intoxicating liquor was drunk with her by him to increase passion. / For some reason or other, on account of her, O best of the twice-born,

2.8.s:
nihatā sā ca pāpena vṛṣalī gatamaṅgalā /
tatastasyāstadā tasya bhrātṛbhirnihataḥ pitā //
2.8.d:
निहता सा च पापेन वृषली गतमङ्गला ।
ततस्तस्यास्तदा तस्य भ्रातृभिर्निहतः पिता ॥
2.8.m: that ill-fated outcaste woman was slain by the wicked man. / Then his father was killed by her brothers.

2.8.s:
mātā ca tasya durbuddherdhaundhumūkasya śobhanā /
bhāryā ca tasya durbuddheḥ śyālāste cāpi suvratāḥ //
2.8.d:
माता च तस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्धौन्धुमूकस्य शोभना ।
भार्या च तस्य दुर्बुद्धेः श्यालास्ते चापि सुव्रताः ॥
2.8.m: And the good mother of that foolish son of Dhundhumūka, / and the wife of that fool, and those brothers-in-law, O you of noble vows,

2.8.s:
rājñā kṣaṇādaho naṣṭa kulaṃ tasyāśca tasya ca /
gatvāsau dhaindhumūkaśca yena kenāpi līlayā //
2.8.d:
राज्ञा क्षणादहो नष्ट कुलं तस्याश्च तस्य च ।
गत्वासौ धैन्धुमूकश्च येन केनापि लीलया ॥
2.8.m: alas, the king instantly destroyed the family of both her and him. / And going away, that son of Dhundhumūka, somehow or other in sport,

2.8.s:
dṛṣṭvā tu taṃ muniśreṣṭhaṃ rudrajāpyaparāyaṇam /
labdhvā pāśupataṃ tadvai purā devānmaheśvarāt //
2.8.d:
दृष्ट्वा तु तं मुनिश्रेष्ठं रुद्रजाप्यपरायणम् ।
लब्ध्वा पाशुपतं तद्वै पुरा देवान्महेश्वरात् ॥
2.8.m: having seen that best of sages devoted to the recitation of Rudra's [mantra], / and having obtained that Pāśupata [observance], formerly [revealed] by the god Maheśvara,

2.8.s:
labdhvā pañcākṣaraṃ caiva ṣaḍakṣaramanuttamam /
punaḥ pañcākṣaraṃ caiva japtvā lakṣaṃ pṛthak pṛthak //
2.8.d:
लब्ध्वा पञ्चाक्षरं चैव षडक्षरमनुत्तमम् ।
पुनः पञ्चाक्षरं चैव जप्त्वा लक्षं पृथक् पृथक् ॥
2.8.m: and having received the five-syllable [mantra] and the unsurpassed six-syllable [mantra], / and having recited again the five-syllable [mantra] a hundred thousand times separately,

2.8.s:
vrataṃ kṛtvā ca vidhinā divyaṃ dvādaśamāsikam /
kāladharmaṃ gataḥ kalpe pūjitaśca yamena vai //
2.8.d:
व्रतं कृत्वा च विधिना दिव्यं द्वादशमासिकम् ।
कालधर्मं गतः कल्पे पूजितश्च यमेन वै ॥
2.8.m: and having performed according to rule the divine twelve-month observance, / passed away in course of time in that kalpa, and was truly worshipped by Yama.

2.8.s:
uddhṛtā ca tathā mātā pitā śyālāśca suvratāḥ /
patnī ca subhagā jātā susmitā ca pativratā //
2.8.d:
उद्धृता च तथा माता पिता श्यालाश्च सुव्रताः ।
पत्नी च सुभगा जाता सुस्मिता च पतिव्रता ॥
2.8.m: And likewise his mother, father, and brothers-in-law of noble vows were delivered, / and his wife became fortunate, sweet-smiling, and devoted to her husband.

2.8.s:
tābhirvimānāmāruhya devaiḥ seṃdrairabhiṣṭutaḥ /
gāṇapatyamanu prāpya rudrasya dayito 'bhavat //
2.8.d:
ताभिर्विमानामारुह्य देवैः सेंद्रैरभिष्टुतः ।
गाणपत्यमनु प्राप्य रुद्रस्य दयितो ऽभवत् ॥
2.8.m: Having mounted an aerial chariot with them, praised by the gods led by Indra, / and having attained leadership among the gaṇas, he became dear to Rudra.

2.8.s:
tasmādaṣṭākṣarāṃnmantrāttathā vai dvādaśākṣarāt /
bhavetkoṭiguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
2.8.d:
तस्मादष्टाक्षरांन्मन्त्रात्तथा वै द्वादशाक्षरात् ।
भवेत्कोटिगुणं पुण्यं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
2.8.m: Therefore, from that eight-syllable mantra and likewise from the twelve-syllable mantra, / the merit is ten-millionfold; there should be no doubt here.

2.8.s:
tasmājjapeddhiyo nityaṃ prāguktena vidhānataḥ /
śaktibījasamāyuktaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim //
2.8.d:
तस्माज्जपेद्धियो नित्यं प्रागुक्तेन विधानतः ।
शक्तिबीजसमायुक्तं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
2.8.m: Therefore, the wise man should continually chant, according to the rule previously stated, / [the mantra] conjoined with the seed-syllable of Śakti; he attains the supreme state.

2.8.s:
etadvaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ kathāsarvasvamuttamam /
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi śrāvayedvā dvijottamān //
2.8.d:
एतद्वः कथितं सर्वं कथासर्वस्वमुत्तमम् ।
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्वापि श्रावयेद्वा द्विजोत्तमान् ॥
2.8.m: This whole essence of the narrative has been told to you, the most excellent [story]. / Whoever recites, listens to, or causes the best of the twice-born to hear it,

2.8.s:
sa yāti brahmalokaṃ tu rudrajāpyamanuttamam //
iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge aṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.8.d:
स याति ब्रह्मलोकं तु रुद्रजाप्यमनुत्तमम् ॥
इति श्रीलिङ्गमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे अष्टमो ऽध्यायः
2.8.m:
he goes to the realm of Brahmā; [this is] the unsurpassed chanting of Rudra.

Thus ends the eighth chapter in the second part of the glorious Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa.

2.9.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
devaiḥ purā kṛtaṃ divyaṃ vrataṃ pāśupataṃ śubham /
brahmaṇā ca svayaṃ sūta kṛṣṇenākliṣṭakarmaṇā //
2.9.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
देवैः पुरा कृतं दिव्यं व्रतं पाशुपतं शुभम् ।
ब्रह्मणा च स्वयं सूत कृष्णेनाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ॥
2.9.m: The sages said: / "Formerly the divine, auspicious Pāśupata observance was performed by the gods, / and by Brahmā himself, O Sūta, and by Kṛṣṇa of untiring deeds,

2.9.s:
patitena ca vipreṇa dhaindhumūkena vai tathā /
kṛtvā japtvā gatiḥ prāptā kathaṃ pāśupataṃ vratam //
2.9.d:
पतितेन च विप्रेण धैन्धुमूकेन वै तथा ।
कृत्वा जप्त्वा गतिः प्राप्ता कथं पाशुपतं व्रतम् ॥
2.9.m: and likewise by the fallen brāhmaṇa, the son of Dhundhumūka. / Having performed and recited what was the goal attained through the Pāśupata observance?

2.9.s:
kathaṃ paśupatirdevaḥ śaṅkaraḥ parameśvaraḥ /
vaktumarhasi cāsmākaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ //
2.9.d:
कथं पशुपतिर्देवः शङ्करः परमेश्वरः ।
वक्तुमर्हसि चास्माकं परं कौतूहलं हि नः ॥
2.9.m: How is the god Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord, Paśupati? / You ought to tell us; indeed our curiosity is great."

2.9.s:
sūta uvāca
purā śāpādvinirmukto brahmaputro mahāyaśāḥ /
rudrasya devadevasya marudeśādihāgataḥ //
2.9.d:
सूत उवाच
पुरा शापाद्विनिर्मुक्तो ब्रह्मपुत्रो महायशाः ।
रुद्रस्य देवदेवस्य मरुदेशादिहागतः ॥
2.9.m: Sūta said: / "Formerly, freed from a curse, the son of Brahmā of great renown, / came here from the desert country of the god of gods, Rudra.

2.9.s:
tyaktvā prasādādrudrasya uṣṭradehamajājñayā /
śilādaputramāsādya namaskṛtya vidhānataḥ //
2.9.d:
त्यक्त्वा प्रसादाद्रुद्रस्य उष्ट्रदेहमजाज्ञया ।
शिलादपुत्रमासाद्य नमस्कृत्य विधानतः ॥
2.9.m: Having shed his camel body by the grace of Rudra and the command of the Unborn, / he approached the son of Śilāda, and having bowed to him according to rule,

2.9.s:
meruṣṭaṣṭhe munivaraḥ śrutvā dharmamanuttamam /
māheśvaraṃ muniśreṣṭhā hyapṛcchacca punaḥ punaḥ //
2.9.d:
मेरुष्टष्ठे मुनिवरः श्रुत्वा धर्ममनुत्तमम् ।
माहेश्वरं मुनिश्रेष्ठा ह्यपृच्छच्च पुनः पुनः ॥
2.9.m: that best of sages, stationed on Meru, having heard the unsurpassed dharma / pertaining to Maheśvara, asked him again and again, O best of sages.

2.9.s:
nandinaṃ praṇipatyainaṃ kathaṃ paśupatiḥ prabhuḥ /
vaktumarhasi cāsmākaṃ tatsarvaṃ ca tadāha saḥ //
2.9.d:
नन्दिनं प्रणिपत्यैनं कथं पशुपतिः प्रभुः ।
वक्तुमर्हसि चास्माकं तत्सर्वं च तदाह सः ॥
2.9.m: Bowing to that Nandin, [he asked,] 'How is the Lord Paśupati? / You ought to tell us all that.' And he then told it [to him].

2.9.s:
tatsarvaṃ śrutavān vyāsaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ prabhuḥ /
tasmādahanumaśrutya yuṣmākaṃ pravadāmi vai //
2.9.d:
तत्सर्वं श्रुतवान् व्यासः कृष्णद्वैपायनः प्रभुः ।
तस्मादहनुमश्रुत्य युष्माकं प्रवदामि वै ॥
2.9.m: The lord Vyāsa, Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, heard all that; / having heard it from him, I tell it truly to you.

2.9.s:
sarve śṛṇvaṃ tu vacanaṃ namaskṛtvā maheśvaram /
sanatkumāra uvāca
kathaṃ paśupatirdevaḥ paśavaḥ ke prakīrtitāḥ //
2.9.d:
सर्वे शृण्वं तु वचनं नमस्कृत्वा महेश्वरम् ।
सनत्कुमार उवाच
कथं पशुपतिर्देवः पशवः के प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
2.9.m: Let all listen to the words, having bowed to Maheśvara. / Sanatkumāra said: / 'How is the god Paśupati? Who are said to be the paśus (beasts)?'

2.9.s:
kaiḥ pāśaiste nibadhyante vimucyante ca te katham /
śailādir uvāca
sanatkumāra vakṣyāmi sarvam etad yathātatham //
2.9.d:
कैः पाशैस्ते निबध्यन्ते विमुच्यन्ते च ते कथम् ।
शैलादिर् उवाच
सनत्कुमार वक्ष्यामि सर्वम् एतद् यथातथम् ॥
2.9.m: 'By what bonds (pāśas) are they bound, and how are they freed?' / The son of Śilāda said: / 'O Sanatkumāra, I shall tell all this as it truly is,

2.9.s:
rudrabhaktasya śāntasya tava kalyāmacetasaḥ /
brahmādyāḥ sthāvarāntāśca devadevasya dhīmataḥ //
2.9.d:
रुद्रभक्तस्य शान्तस्य तव कल्यामचेतसः ।
ब्रह्माद्याः स्थावरान्ताश्च देवदेवस्य धीमतः ॥
2.9.m: to you who are a devotee of Rudra, tranquil, and of auspicious mind. / From Brahmā down to immobile creatures, of the wise God of gods,

2.9.s:
paśavaḥ parikīrtyante saṃsāravaśavartinaḥ /
teṣāṃ patitvādbhagavān rudraḥ paśupatiḥ smṛtaḥ //
2.9.d:
पशवः परिकीर्त्यन्ते संसारवशवर्तिनः ।
तेषां पतित्वाद्भगवान् रुद्रः पशुपतिः स्मृतः ॥
2.9.m: they are declared to be paśus, subject to the power of transmigration. / Because of his lordship over them, Lord Rudra is recalled as Paśupati.

2.9.s:
anādinidhano dhātā bhagavānviṣṇuravyayaḥ /
māyāpāśena badhnāti paśuvatparameśvaraḥ //
2.9.d:
अनादिनिधनो धाता भगवान्विष्णुरव्ययः ।
मायापाशेन बध्नाति पशुवत्परमेश्वरः ॥
2.9.m: The creator, Lord Viṣṇu, who is imperishable, without beginning or end, / the Supreme Lord binds like a beast with the bond of māyā.

2.9.s:
sa eva mocakasteṣāṃ jñānayogena sevitaḥ /
avidyāpāśabaddhānāṃ nānyo mocaka iṣyate //
2.9.d:
स एव मोचकस्तेषां ज्ञानयोगेन सेवितः ।
अविद्यापाशबद्धानां नान्यो मोचक इष्यते ॥
2.9.m: He alone is their liberator when served through the yoga of knowledge; / for those bound by the bond of ignorance, no other liberator is recognized

2.9.s:
tamṛte paramātmānaṃ śaṅkaraṃ parameśvaram /
caturviṃśatitattvāni pāśā hi parameṣṭhinaḥ //
2.9.d:
तमृते परमात्मानं शङ्करं परमेश्वरम् ।
चतुर्विंशतितत्त्वानि पाशा हि परमेष्ठिनः ॥
2.9.m: except that Supreme Self, Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord. / The twenty-four principles are indeed the bonds of the Supreme Deity.

2.9.s:
taiḥ pāśairmocayatyekaḥ śivo jīvairupāsitaḥ /
nibadhnāti paśūnekaścaturviṃśatipāśakaiḥ //
2.9.d:
तैः पाशैर्मोचयत्येकः शिवो जीवैरुपासितः ।
निबध्नाति पशूनेकश्चतुर्विंशतिपाशकैः ॥
2.9.m: By means of those bonds the one Śiva, worshipped by individual souls, liberates them; / he alone binds the paśus by means of the twenty-four bonds.

2.9.s:
sa eva bhagavānrudro mocayatyapi sevitaḥ /
daśendriyamayaiḥ pāśairantaḥ karaṇasaṃbhavaiḥ //
2.9.d:
स एव भगवान्रुद्रो मोचयत्यपि सेवितः ।
दशेन्द्रियमयैः पाशैरन्तः करणसंभवैः ॥
2.9.m: That very Lord Rudra also liberates them when served. / By bonds consisting of the ten senses and originating in the inner instrument,

2.9.s:
bhūtatanmātrapāśaiśca paśūnmocayati prabhuḥ /
indriyārthamayaiḥ pāśair baddhvā viṣayinaḥ prabhuḥ //
2.9.d:
भूततन्मात्रपाशैश्च पशून्मोचयति प्रभुः ।
इन्द्रियार्थमयैः पाशैर् बद्ध्वा विषयिनः प्रभुः ॥
2.9.m: and by bonds of the subtle elements of the gross elements, the Lord liberates the paśus. / Having bound the sense-indulgent with bonds composed of the objects of the senses, the Lord—

2.9.s:
āśu bhaktā bhavantyevaṃ parameśvarasevayā /
bhaja ityeṣa dhātur vai sevāyāṃ parikīrtitaḥ //
2.9.d:
आशु भक्ता भवन्त्येवं परमेश्वरसेवया ।
भज इत्येष धातुर् वै सेवायां परिकीर्तितः ॥
2.9.m: thus they quickly become devotees through service to the Supreme Lord. / The verbal root 'bhaj' is indeed proclaimed in the sense of service.

2.9.s:
tasmātsevā budhaiḥ proktā bhaktiśabdena bhūyasī /
brahmadistaṃbaparyantaṃ paśūnbaddhvā maheśvaraḥ //
2.9.d:
तस्मात्सेवा बुधैः प्रोक्ता भक्तिशब्देन भूयसी ।
ब्रह्मदिस्तंबपर्यन्तं पशून्बद्ध्वा महेश्वरः ॥
2.9.m: Therefore, service is designated as great by the wise with the word 'bhakti'. / Having bound the paśus from Brahmā down to a clump of grass,

2.9.s:
tribhirguṇamayaiḥ pāśaiḥ kāryaṃ kārayati svayam /
dṛḍhena bhaktiyogena paśubhiḥ samupāsitaḥ //
2.9.d:
त्रिभिर्गुणमयैः पाशैः कार्यं कारयति स्वयम् ।
दृढेन भक्तियोगेन पशुभिः समुपासितः ॥
2.9.m: Maheśvara himself causes actions to be done through the bonds composed of the three guṇas. / Fully worshipped by the paśus with firm bhakti-yoga,

2.9.s:
mocayatyeva tānsadyaḥ śaṅkaraḥ parameśvaraḥ /
bhajanaṃ bhaktirityuktā vāṅmanaḥ kāyakarmabhiḥ //
2.9.d:
मोचयत्येव तान्सद्यः शङ्करः परमेश्वरः ।
भजनं भक्तिरित्युक्ता वाङ्मनः कायकर्मभिः ॥
2.9.m: Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord, instantly liberates them. / Worship through actions of speech, mind, and body is called bhakti.

2.9.s:
sarvakāryeṇahetutvātpāśacchedapaṭīyasī /
satyaḥ sarvaga ityādi śivasya guṇacintanā //
2.9.d:
सर्वकार्येणहेतुत्वात्पाशच्छेदपटीयसी ।
सत्यः सर्वग इत्यादि शिवस्य गुणचिन्तना ॥
2.9.m: Being the cause of all achievements, it is most adept at cutting the bond. / Meditation on the qualities of Śiva, such as 'He is truth, all-pervading,' etc.,

2.9.s:
rupopādānacintā ca mānasaṃ bhajanaṃ viduḥ /
vācikaṃ bhajanaṃ dhīrāḥ praṇavādijapaṃ viduḥ //
2.9.d:
रुपोपादानचिन्ता च मानसं भजनं विदुः ।
वाचिकं भजनं धीराः प्रणवादिजपं विदुः ॥
2.9.m: and contemplation on his assumed form, they know as mental worship. / The wise know vocal worship to be the chanting of the Praṇava and other [mantras].

2.9.s:
kāyikaṃ bhajanaṃ sadbhiḥ prāṇāyāmādi kathyate /
dharmādharmamayaiḥ pāśairbandhanaṃ dehināmidam //
2.9.d:
कायिकं भजनं सद्भिः प्राणायामादि कथ्यते ।
धर्माधर्ममयैः पाशैर्बन्धनं देहिनामिदम् ॥
2.9.m: Bodily worship is declared by the virtuous to be breath-control and the like. / This bondage of embodied beings is through bonds composed of dharma and adharma.

2.9.s:
mocakaḥ śiva evaiko bhagavānparameśvaraḥ /
caturviśatitattvāni māyākarmaguṇā iti //
2.9.d:
मोचकः शिव एवैको भगवान्परमेश्वरः ।
चतुर्विशतितत्त्वानि मायाकर्मगुणा इति ॥
2.9.m: The only liberator is Śiva alone, the Blessed Lord, the Supreme Sovereign. / The twenty-four principles, māyā, action, and the guṇas—

2.9.s:
kīrtyante viṣayāśceti pāśā jīvanibandhanāt /
tairbaddhāḥ śivabhaktyaiva mucyante sarvadehinaḥ //
2.9.d:
कीर्त्यन्ते विषयाश्चेति पाशा जीवनिबन्धनात् ।
तैर्बद्धाः शिवभक्त्यैव मुच्यन्ते सर्वदेहिनः ॥
2.9.m: as well as the sense objects—are declared to be bonds because they bind the individual soul. / Bound by them, all embodied beings are liberated solely through devotion to Śiva.

2.9.s:
pañcakleśamayaiḥ pāśaiḥ paśūnbadhnāti śaṅkaraḥ /
sa eva mocakastoṣāṃ bhaktyā samyagupāsitaḥ //
2.9.d:
पञ्चक्लेशमयैः पाशैः पशून्बध्नाति शङ्करः ।
स एव मोचकस्तोषां भक्त्या सम्यगुपासितः ॥
2.9.m: Śaṅkara binds the individual souls with bonds consisting of the five afflictions. / He alone is their liberator when duly worshipped with devotion.

2.9.s:
avidyāmasmitāṃ rāgaṃ dveṣaṃ ca dvipadāṃ varāḥ /
vadantyabhiniveśaṃ ca kleśānpāśatvamāgatān //
2.9.d:
अविद्यामस्मितां रागं द्वेषं च द्विपदां वराः ।
वदन्त्यभिनिवेशं च क्लेशान्पाशत्वमागतान् ॥
2.9.m: Ignorance, egoism, attachment, aversion, / and clinging to life, O best of men, they declare to be the afflictions that have become bonds.

2.9.s:
tamomohomahāmohastāmisra iti paṇḍitāḥ /
andhatāmisra ityāhuravidyāṃ pañcadhā sthitām //
2.9.d:
तमोमोहोमहामोहस्तामिस्र इति पण्डिताः ।
अन्धतामिस्र इत्याहुरविद्यां पञ्चधा स्थिताम् ॥
2.9.m: The learned declare ignorance to exist in five forms: / darkness, delusion, great delusion, gloom, and blinding gloom.

2.9.s:
tāñjīvānmuniśārdūlāḥ sarvāṃścaivāpyavidyayā /
śivo mocayati śrīmānnānyaḥ kaścidvimocakaḥ //
2.9.d:
ताञ्जीवान्मुनिशार्दूलाः सर्वांश्चैवाप्यविद्यया ।
शिवो मोचयति श्रीमान्नान्यः कश्चिद्विमोचकः ॥
2.9.m: From ignorance, O tigers among sages, glorious Śiva / liberates all those souls; there is no other liberator.

2.9.s:
avidyāṃ tama ityāhurasmitāṃ moha ityapi /
mahāmoha iti prājñā rāgaṃ yogaparāyaṇāḥ //
2.9.d:
अविद्यां तम इत्याहुरस्मितां मोह इत्यपि ।
महामोह इति प्राज्ञा रागं योगपरायणाः ॥
2.9.m: The wise devoted to yoga call ignorance 'darkness', egoism 'delusion', / and attachment 'great delusion'.

2.9.s:
dveṣaṃ tāmisra ityāhurandhatāmisra ityapi /
tathaivābhiniveśaṃ ca mithyājñānaṃ vivekinaḥ //
2.9.d:
द्वेषं तामिस्र इत्याहुरन्धतामिस्र इत्यपि ।
तथैवाभिनिवेशं च मिथ्याज्ञानं विवेकिनः ॥
2.9.m: The discerning call aversion 'gloom', and likewise clinging to life / they call 'blinding gloom' and false knowledge.

2.9.s:
tamaso 'ṣṭavidhā bhedā mohaścāṣṭavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ /
mahāmohaprabhedāśca budhairdaśa vicintitāḥ //
2.9.d:
तमसो ऽष्टविधा भेदा मोहश्चाष्टविधः स्मृतः ।
महामोहप्रभेदाश्च बुधैर्दश विचिन्तिताः ॥
2.9.m: The varieties of darkness are eightfold, and delusion is considered eightfold; / the varieties of great delusion have been determined by the wise to be ten.

2.9.s:
aṣṭādaśavidhaṃ cāhustāmisraṃ ca vicakṣaṇāḥ /
andhatāmisrabhedāśca tathāṣṭādaśadhā smṛtāḥ //
2.9.d:
अष्टादशविधं चाहुस्तामिस्रं च विचक्षणाः ।
अन्धतामिस्रभेदाश्च तथाष्टादशधा स्मृताः ॥
2.9.m: The discerning declare gloom to be eighteenfold, / and the varieties of blinding gloom are likewise recorded as eighteenfold.

2.9.s:
avidyayāsya saṃbandho nātīto nāstyanāgataḥ /
bhavedrāgeṇa devasya śaṃbhoraṅganivāsinaḥ //
2.9.d:
अविद्ययास्य संबन्धो नातीतो नास्त्यनागतः ।
भवेद्रागेण देवस्य शंभोरङ्गनिवासिनः ॥
2.9.m: He has no connection with ignorance, neither past nor future. / Nor can there be any connection through attachment for the God, Śambhu, who abides within his own nature.

2.9.s:
kāleṣu triṣu saṃbandhastasya dveṣeṇa no bhavet /
māyātītasya devasya sthāṇoḥ paśupatervibhoḥ //
2.9.d:
कालेषु त्रिषु संबन्धस्तस्य द्वेषेण नो भवेत् ।
मायातीतस्य देवस्य स्थाणोः पशुपतेर्विभोः ॥
2.9.m: In the three times, he can have no connection with aversion— / the God beyond māyā, Sthāṇu, Paśupati, the all-pervading Lord.

2.9.s:
tathaivābhiniveśena saṃbandho na kadācana /
śaṅkarasya śaraṇyasya śivasya paramātmanaḥ //
2.9.d:
तथैवाभिनिवेशेन संबन्धो न कदाचन ।
शङ्करस्य शरण्यस्य शिवस्य परमात्मनः ॥
2.9.m: Likewise, there is never any connection through clinging to life / for Śaṅkara, the refuge, Śiva, the Supreme Self.

2.9.s:
kuśalākuśalaistasya saṃbandho naiva karmabhiḥ /
bhavetkālatraye śaṃbhoravidyāmativartinaḥ //
2.9.d:
कुशलाकुशलैस्तस्य संबन्धो नैव कर्मभिः ।
भवेत्कालत्रये शंभोरविद्यामतिवर्तिनः ॥
2.9.m: He has no connection whatsoever with virtuous or unvirtuous actions / in the three times—Śambhu who transcends ignorance.

2.9.s:
vipākaiḥ karmaṇāṃ vāpi na bhavedeva saṃgamaḥ /
kāleṣu triṣu sarvasya śivasya śivadāyinaḥ //
2.9.d:
विपाकैः कर्मणां वापि न भवेदेव संगमः ।
कालेषु त्रिषु सर्वस्य शिवस्य शिवदायिनः ॥
2.9.m: Nor is there ever any contact with the fruits of actions / in the three times for Śiva, the all, the giver of auspiciousness.

2.9.s:
sukhaduḥkhairasaṃspṛśyaḥ kālatritayavartibhiḥ /
sa tair vinaśvaraiḥ śaṃbhur bodhānandātmakaḥ paraḥ //
2.9.d:
सुखदुःखैरसंस्पृश्यः कालत्रितयवर्तिभिः ।
स तैर् विनश्वरैः शंभुर् बोधानन्दात्मकः परः ॥
2.9.m: Untouchable by pleasures and pains existing in the triad of times, / by those perishable things, Śambhu is the supreme, consisting of consciousness and bliss.

2.9.s:
āśayairaparāmṛṣṭaḥ kālatritayagocaraiḥ /
dhiyāṃ patiḥ svabhūreṣa mahādevo maheśvaraḥ //
2.9.d:
आशयैरपरामृष्टः कालत्रितयगोचरैः ।
धियां पतिः स्वभूरेष महादेवो महेश्वरः ॥
2.9.m: Uncontacted by latencies within the range of the triad of times, / he is the lord of intellects, self-born, Mahādeva, Maheśvara.

2.9.s:
aspṛśyaḥ karmasaṃskāraiḥ kālatritayavartibhiḥ /
tathaiva bhogasaṃskārairbhagavānantakāntakaḥ //
2.9.d:
अस्पृश्यः कर्मसंस्कारैः कालत्रितयवर्तिभिः ।
तथैव भोगसंस्कारैर्भगवानन्तकान्तकः ॥
2.9.m: Untouchable by the subliminal impressions of karma existing in the triad of times, / and likewise by the subliminal impressions of experience, is the Blessed Lord, the destroyer of Antaka.

2.9.s:
puṃviśeṣaparo devo bhagavānparameśvaraḥ /
ceta nācetanāyuktaprapañcādakhilātparaḥ //
2.9.d:
पुंविशेषपरो देवो भगवान्परमेश्वरः ।
चेत नाचेतनायुक्तप्रपञ्चादखिलात्परः ॥
2.9.m: The God, the Blessed Lord, the Supreme Sovereign, is higher than any distinct puruṣa, / beyond the entire manifest universe composed of the conscious and the unconscious.

2.9.s:
loke sātiśayatvena jñānaiśvaryaṃ vilokyate /
śivenātiśayatvena śivaṃ prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ //
2.9.d:
लोके सातिशयत्वेन ज्ञानैश्वर्यं विलोक्यते ।
शिवेनातिशयत्वेन शिवं प्राहुर्मनीषिणः ॥
2.9.m: In the world, knowledge and sovereignty are seen to possess degrees of excellence; / the wise speak of Śiva as Śiva because of his unsurpassable excellence.

2.9.s:
pratisargaṃ prasūtānāṃ brahmaṇaṃ śāstravistaram /
upadeṣṭā sa evādau kālāvacchedavartinām //
2.9.d:
प्रतिसर्गं प्रसूतानां ब्रह्मणं शास्त्रविस्तरम् ।
उपदेष्टा स एवादौ कालावच्छेदवर्तिनाम् ॥
2.9.m: He alone was in the beginning the teacher of the multitude of scriptures / to Brahmā and the others born at each creation, who are subject to the limitation of time.

2.9.s:
kālāvacchedayuktānāṃ gurūṇāmapyasau guruḥ /
sarveṣāmeva sarveśaḥ kālāvacchedavarjitaḥ //
2.9.d:
कालावच्छेदयुक्तानां गुरूणामप्यसौ गुरुः ।
सर्वेषामेव सर्वेशः कालावच्छेदवर्जितः ॥
2.9.m: He is the teacher even of the teachers who are subject to the limitation of time, / the Lord of all beings, completely devoid of the limitation of time.

2.9.s:
anādireṣa saṃbandho vijñānotkarṣayoḥ paraḥ /
sthitayorīdṛśaḥ sarvaḥ pariśuddhaḥ svabhāvataḥ //
2.9.d:
अनादिरेष संबन्धो विज्ञानोत्कर्षयोः परः ।
स्थितयोरीदृशः सर्वः परिशुद्धः स्वभावतः ॥
2.9.m: This supreme connection between knowledge and pre-eminence is beginningless; / abiding thus, he is all, completely pure by nature.

2.9.s:
ātmaprayojanābhāve parānugraha eva hi /
prayojanaṃ samastānāṃ kāryāṇāṃ parameśvaraḥ //
2.9.d:
आत्मप्रयोजनाभावे परानुग्रह एव हि ।
प्रयोजनं समस्तानां कार्याणां परमेश्वरः ॥
2.9.m: Since he has no purpose of his own, grace toward others is indeed / the sole purpose of all the actions of the Supreme Sovereign.

2.9.s:
praṇavo vācakastasya śivasya paramātmanaḥ /
śivarudrādiśabdānāṃ praṇavopi paraḥ smṛtaḥ //
2.9.d:
प्रणवो वाचकस्तस्य शिवस्य परमात्मनः ।
शिवरुद्रादिशब्दानां प्रणवोपि परः स्मृतः ॥
2.9.m: The syllable Oṃ is the expressive word for that Śiva, the Supreme Self; / even among words like Śiva and Rudra, the syllable Oṃ is considered supreme.

2.9.s:
śaṃbhoḥ praṇavavācyasya bhāvanā tajjapādapi /
yā siddhiḥ svaparāprāpyā bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ //
2.9.d:
शंभोः प्रणववाच्यस्य भावना तज्जपादपि ।
या सिद्धिः स्वपराप्राप्या भवत्येव न संशयः ॥
2.9.m: From meditation upon Śambhu, who is expressed by the syllable Oṃ, and from recitation of it, / that perfection which is inaccessible to oneself and others definitely arises, without doubt.

2.9.s:
jñānatattvaṃ prayatnena yogaḥ pāśupataḥ paraḥ /
uktastu devadevena sarveṣāmanukaṃpayā //
2.9.d:
ज्ञानतत्त्वं प्रयत्नेन योगः पाशुपतः परः ।
उक्तस्तु देवदेवेन सर्वेषामनुकंपया ॥
2.9.m: The reality of knowledge [and] the supreme Pāśupata yoga / have been taught with great care by the God of gods out of compassion for all.

2.9.s:
sa hovācaiva yājñavalkyo yadakṣaraṃ gārgyayoginaḥ /
abhivadanti sthūlamanantaṃ mahāścaryamadīrghamalohitamamastakamāsāyamata evo punānasamasaṃgamagandhamarasamackṣuṣkamaśrotramavāṅmanotejaskamapramāṇamanusukhamanāmagotramamaramajaramanāmayamamṛtamoṃśabdamamṛtamasaṃvṛtamapūrvamanaparamanantamabāhyaṃ tadaśrāti kiñcana na tāśrāti kiñcana //
2.9.d:
स होवाचैव याज्ञवल्क्यो यदक्षरं गार्ग्ययोगिनः ।
अभिवदन्ति स्थूलमनन्तं महाश्चर्यमदीर्घमलोहितममस्तकमासायमत एवो पुनानसमसंगमगन्धमरसमच्क्षुष्कमश्रोत्रमवाङ्मनोतेजस्कमप्रमाणमनुसुखमनामगोत्रममरमजरमनामयममृतमोंशब्दममृतमसंवृतमपूर्वमनपरमनन्तमबाह्यं तदश्राति किञ्चन न ताश्राति किञ्चन ॥
2.9.m: Yājñavalkya indeed said: That Imperishable which the yogins, O Gārgī, / declare to be not gross, endless, greatly wondrous, not long, not red, headless, foundationless, therefore purifying, odorless, unattached, scentless, tasteless, eyeless, earless, without speech, without mind, without heat, measureless, following bliss, without name or family, deathless, ageless, free from illness, immortal, the sound Oṃ, immortal, uncovered, without before, without after, endless, without outside; it consumes nothing, and nothing consumes it.

2.9.s:
etatkālavyaye jñātvā paraṃ pāśupataṃ prabhum /
yoge pāśupate cāsmin yasyārthaḥ kila uttame //
2.9.d:
एतत्कालव्यये ज्ञात्वा परं पाशुपतं प्रभुम् ।
योगे पाशुपते चास्मिन् यस्यार्थः किल उत्तमे ॥
2.9.m: Having known this supreme Pāśupata Lord at the end of time, / and in this supreme Pāśupata yoga whose meaning [is declared]—

2.9.s:
kṛtvoṅkāraṃ pradīpaṃ mṛgaya gṛhapatiṃ sūkṣmamādyantarasthaṃ saṃyamya dvāravāsaṃ pavanapaṭutaraṃ nāyakaṃ condriyāṇām /
vāgjālaiḥ kasya hetorvibhaṭasi tu bhayaṃ dṛśyate naiva kiñciddehasthaṃ paśya śaṃbhuṃ bhramasi kimu pare sāstrajālendhakāre //
2.9.d:
कृत्वोङ्कारं प्रदीपं मृगय गृहपतिं सूक्ष्ममाद्यन्तरस्थं संयम्य द्वारवासं पवनपटुतरं नायकं चोन्द्रियाणाम् ।
वाग्जालैः कस्य हेतोर्विभटसि तु भयं दृश्यते नैव किञ्चिद्देहस्थं पश्य शंभुं भ्रमसि किमु परे सास्त्रजालेन्धकारे ॥
2.9.m: Having made the syllable Oṃ a lamp, search for the master of the house, subtle, dwelling between beginning and end, having restrained the wind dwelling at the gates, which is very swift, and the leader of the senses; / for what reason do you become bewildered by webs of words? Truly no fear is seen at all. Behold Śambhu residing in the body; why do you wander in the darkness of the web of other treatises?

2.9.s:
evaṃ samyagbudhairjñātvā munīnāmatha coktaṃ śivena /
asamarasaṃ pañcadhā kṛtvābhavaṃ cātmani yojayet //
iti śrīliṃṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge navamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.9.d:
एवं सम्यग्बुधैर्ज्ञात्वा मुनीनामथ चोक्तं शिवेन ।
असमरसं पञ्चधा कृत्वाभवं चात्मनि योजयेत् ॥
इति श्रीलिंङ्गमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे नवमो ऽध्यायः
2.9.m:
Thus, having properly understood, it was spoken by Śiva to the sages: / having divided the peerless essence into five parts, one should unite Bhava with oneself.

Thus ends the ninth chapter in the Uttarabhāga of the glorious Liṅgamahāpurāṇa.

2.10.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
bhūya eva mamācakṣva mahimānamumāpateḥ /
bhavabhakta mahāprājña bhagavannandikeśvara //
2.10.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
भूय एव ममाचक्ष्व महिमानमुमापतेः ।
भवभक्त महाप्राज्ञ भगवन्नन्दिकेश्वर ॥
2.10.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Tell me further of the greatness of the Lord of Umā, / O devotee of Bhava, O highly wise one, O blessed Nandikeśvara.

2.10.s:
śailādiruvāca
sanatkumāra saṃkṣepāttava vakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ /
mahimānaṃ maheśasya bhavasya parameṣṭhinaḥ //
2.10.d:
शैलादिरुवाच
सनत्कुमार संक्षेपात्तव वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः ।
महिमानं महेशस्य भवस्य परमेष्ठिनः ॥
2.10.m: The son of Śilāda said: / Sanatkumāra, I shall tell you briefly and in its entirety / the greatness of Maheśa, Bhava, the Supreme Lord.

2.10.s:
nāsya prakṛtibandho 'bhūdbuddhibandho na kaścana /
na cāhaṅkārabandhaśca manobandhaśca no 'bhavat //
2.10.d:
नास्य प्रकृतिबन्धो ऽभूद्बुद्धिबन्धो न कश्चन ।
न चाहङ्कारबन्धश्च मनोबन्धश्च नो ऽभवत् ॥
2.10.m: He had no bondage to prakṛti, no bondage to intellect, / no bondage to ego, and no bondage to mind.

2.10.s:
cittabandho na tasyābhūcchrotrabandho na cābhavat /
na tvacāṃ cakṣuṣāṃ vāpi bandho jajñe kadācana //
2.10.d:
चित्तबन्धो न तस्याभूच्छ्रोत्रबन्धो न चाभवत् ।
न त्वचां चक्षुषां वापि बन्धो जज्ञे कदाचन ॥
2.10.m: He had no bondage to the faculty of thought, and no bondage to the ears; / nor did any bondage of the skin or eyes ever arise for him.

2.10.s:
jihvābandho na tasyābhūdghrāṇabandho na kaścana /
pādabandhaḥ pāṇibandho vāgbandhaścaiva suvrata //
2.10.d:
जिह्वाबन्धो न तस्याभूद्घ्राणबन्धो न कश्चन ।
पादबन्धः पाणिबन्धो वाग्बन्धश्चैव सुव्रत ॥
2.10.m: He had no bondage of the tongue, nor any bondage of the nose, / nor bondage of the feet, bondage of the hands, or bondage of speech, O one of good vows,

2.10.s:
upasthendriya bandhaśca bhūtatanmātrabandhanam /
nityaśuddhasvabhāvena nityabuddho nisargataḥ //
2.10.d:
उपस्थेन्द्रिय बन्धश्च भूततन्मात्रबन्धनम् ।
नित्यशुद्धस्वभावेन नित्यबुद्धो निसर्गतः ॥
2.10.m: nor bondage of the genital organ, nor bondage of the elements and subtle elements; / through his eternally pure nature, he is eternally awakened by nature.

2.10.s:
nityamukta iti prokto munibhistattvavedibhiḥ /
anādi madhyaniṣṭhasya śivasya parameṣṭhinaḥ //
2.10.d:
नित्यमुक्त इति प्रोक्तो मुनिभिस्तत्त्ववेदिभिः ।
अनादि मध्यनिष्ठस्य शिवस्य परमेष्ठिनः ॥
2.10.m: He is called 'eternally free' by the sages who know reality; / of Śiva, the Supreme Lord, who is established without beginning or middle,

2.10.s:
buddhiṃ sūte niyogena prakṛtiḥ puruṣasya ca /
ahaṅkāraṃ prasūte 'syā buddhistasya niyogataḥ //
2.10.d:
बुद्धिं सूते नियोगेन प्रकृतिः पुरुषस्य च ।
अहङ्कारं प्रसूते ऽस्या बुद्धिस्तस्य नियोगतः ॥
2.10.m: prakṛti brings forth the intellect and puruṣa by his command; / from this intellect of his, ego is brought forth by his command.

2.10.s:
antaryāmīti deheṣu prasiddhasya svayaṃbhuvaḥ /
indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ ca tanmātrāṇi ca śāsanāt //
2.10.d:
अन्तर्यामीति देहेषु प्रसिद्धस्य स्वयंभुवः ।
इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च तन्मात्राणि च शासनात् ॥
2.10.m: Of the self-born one, well known as the inner controller within bodies, / the eleven senses and the subtle elements are produced by the decree

2.10.s:
ahaṅkāro 'tisaṃsūte śivasya parameṣṭhinaḥ /
tanmātrāṇi niyogena tasya saṃsuvate prabho //
2.10.d:
अहङ्कारो ऽतिसंसूते शिवस्य परमेष्ठिनः ।
तन्मात्राणि नियोगेन तस्य संसुवते प्रभो ॥
2.10.m: of Śiva, the Supreme Lord; ego brings them forth abundantly. / By his command, O lord, the subtle elements bring forth

2.10.s:
mahābhūtānyaśeṣeṇa mahādevasya dhīmataḥ /
brahmādīnāṃ tṛṇāntaṃ hi dehināṃ dehasaṃgatim //
2.10.d:
महाभूतान्यशेषेण महादेवस्य धीमतः ।
ब्रह्मादीनां तृणान्तं हि देहिनां देहसंगतिम् ॥
2.10.m: all the gross elements of the wise Mahādeva. / For all embodied beings, from Brahmā down to a blade of grass, union with a body

2.10.s:
mahābhūtānyaśeṣāṇi janayanti śivājñayā /
adhyavasyati sarvārthānbuddhistasyājñayā vibhoḥ //
2.10.d:
महाभूतान्यशेषाणि जनयन्ति शिवाज्ञया ।
अध्यवस्यति सर्वार्थान्बुद्धिस्तस्याज्ञया विभोः ॥
2.10.m: is produced by all the gross elements at the command of Śiva. / The intellect ascertains all objects by the command of that all-pervading Lord.

2.10.s:
antaryāmīti deheṣu prasiddhasya svayaṃbhuvaḥ /
svabhāvasiddhamaiśvaryaṃ svabhāvādeva bhūtayaḥ //
2.10.d:
अन्तर्यामीति देहेषु प्रसिद्धस्य स्वयंभुवः ।
स्वभावसिद्धमैश्वर्यं स्वभावादेव भूतयः ॥
2.10.m: Of the Self-born One, well-known as the Inner Controller within bodies, / sovereign power is natural, and prosperities arise from His very nature.

2.10.s:
tasyājñayā samastārthānahaṅkāro 'timanyate /
cittaṃ cetayate cāpi manaḥ saṃkalpayatyapi //
2.10.d:
तस्याज्ञया समस्तार्थानहङ्कारो ऽतिमन्यते ।
चित्तं चेतयते चापि मनः संकल्पयत्यपि ॥
2.10.m: By His command, the ego-sense conceives all objects; / the intellect perceives, and the mind forms intentions.

2.10.s:
śrotraṃ śṛṇoti tacchaktyā śabdasparśādikaṃ ca yat /
śaṃbhorājñabalenaiva bhavasya parameṣṭhinaḥ //
2.10.d:
श्रोत्रं शृणोति तच्छक्त्या शब्दस्पर्शादिकं च यत् ।
शंभोराज्ञबलेनैव भवस्य परमेष्ठिनः ॥
